current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice (DC). No
stronger choice principle is assumed. Use a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented underlying four-manifold with a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $(M,g,N,o)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$,
curvature convention, length coordinates $x^0=ct$, and SI assignments of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Fix $c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$,
$\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an
open interval $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values
of $|\varphi|^2$. The classical domain is [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]: the model uses a $C^2$ complex scalar $\varphi$ and a
globally defined real $C^2$ one-form $A$ with $F=dA$. The smooth configurations are retained as a subclass. In length coordinates
$[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, $[\lambda]=\mathrm{Wb^{-1}}$,
$[K_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, and $[V]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

Adopt the explicit classical compact-interior stationary total action of
[[post-emg-trivial-classical-charged-scalar-model]]. The same declared classical action includes smooth configurations; no integer-weight circle representation is assumed for arbitrary real $\lambda$.
Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and
$P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi$. For a charged covector set
$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b$, where $\nabla$ is the
spacetime Levi-Civita derivative; indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. The scalar
equation, current and Hilbert tensor are

$$E_\varphi:=\mathcal D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}\bigl(g^{cd}\overline{P_c}P_d+V(|\varphi|^2)\bigr).$$

Set $T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd})$,
$T^{\mathrm{tot}}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$, and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The equations of the adopted action model are

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}_{ab},\qquad E_\varphi=0.$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial hypersurface, $h$ its induced
Riemannian metric, $n$ its future unit normal, and
$\mathcal K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ its second fundamental form. Let
$\nabla^\Sigma$ denote the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$ and
$\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_h\mathcal K$.
Let $i_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion. The complete scalar
data are $\varphi_0:=\varphi|_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i:=(\mathcal D_i\varphi)|_\Sigma$, and the independently prescribed
$\pi_n:=n^a\mathcal D_a\varphi|_\Sigma$. In a spatial chart this means
$\pi_i=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$. The globally
defined spatial potential is $A_\Sigma:=i_\Sigma^*A$, with exact-potential
compatibility $F|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. Use the temporal potential
gauge $A_0:=A(\partial_0)=0$ in local normal coordinates with $\partial_0=n$
initially, so $A(n)=0$ on $\Sigma$ and $\pi_0=\pi_n$ initially.

For the periodic high-regularity branch take
$\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with
dimensionless periodic coordinates $y^i$, and fix $L_0>0$ metres so that the
length coordinates are $x^i=L_0y^i$. Sobolev norms use $y$; tensor components
and derivative units use the length coordinates $x$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer. Prescribe a
Riemannian metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous
representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric
$\mathcal K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real
$A_\Sigma\in H^s$, $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex
$\pi_n\in H^s$. Here the Sobolev spaces are componentwise real, with complex
components split into real and imaginary parts. For the periodic state, let
$(\mathsf e_A(h))_{A=1}^3$ be the positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame
obtained by Gram–Schmidt from the ordered global length-coordinate frame, as
specified in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Put
$\widehat e_A:=h(e,\mathsf e_A(h))$ and
$\widehat b_A:=h(b,\mathsf e_A(h))$. The initial two-form convention below
then gives $F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),n)=\widehat e_A$ and
$F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),\mathsf e_B(h))=\epsilon_{ABC}\widehat b_C$, with
$\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Thus $\widehat e_A=E_A/c$ and
$\widehat b_A=B_A$ in the observer convention of [[def-emg-geometry-units]],
and both components have unit tesla. Sobolev regularity of the vector fields
$e,b$ refers to their components in the fixed periodic coordinates; the
orthonormal-frame state components are those specified by the named convention.
The initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ is fixed by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. Assume
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$ and
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. With $j,T^{\mathrm{tot}}$
evaluated on the complete initial fields, impose the Maxwell constraints

$$\nabla^\Sigma_i b^i=0,\qquad \nabla^\Sigma_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad j^0:=-n_aj^a,$$

and the Einstein constraints in the stated sign convention,

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|\mathcal K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X)-\nabla^\Sigma_X\tau=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma).$$

Here $(\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X):=h^{ij}(\nabla^\Sigma_{\partial_i}\mathcal K)(\partial_j,X)$, so the momentum equation is an equality of covectors and does not mix coordinate and orthonormal components.

Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ on $\Sigma$ and the product
comparison metric $\bar g:=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. Define
$H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$ and
$Q^i:=h^{jk}(\Gamma(h)^i{}_{jk}-\Gamma(\gamma)^i{}_{jk})$. Use the initial
harmonic metric jet

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2\mathcal K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\tau,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}Q^j.$$

Let $\bar\nabla$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $\bar g$ and put
$p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$ for the
first-order metric derivative variables. For a fixed field scale $F_0>0$
tesla, form the real first-order state from
$(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$, the six orthonormal-frame Maxwell components
$(\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A)$, the three spatial potential components $A_i$,
and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. Rescale each first
metric derivative and each $\pi_a$ by multiplying by $L_0$, each
$\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A$ by dividing by $F_0$, and each $A_i$ by dividing
by $L_0F_0$; $g_{ab}$ and $\varphi$ are already
dimensionless. These fixed invertible scales are bookkeeping choices, not
extra equations. Denote the resulting componentwise-real periodic state by
$u_0$. Suppose its continuous range is a compact $K_0$ contained in the
interior of a compact $K_1$ inside an open admissible state set $O$, that the
coefficient maps are smooth on $O$, the potential range lies in $\mathcal U$,
and the combined time matrix is positive definite throughout $O$. Require
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ for some finite $R\ge0$. Thus
$u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K_0,R)$ in the componentwise real periodic Fourier and
weak-derivative convention used by the CP04 supplier.

Under the stated mathematical hypotheses of the current authored supplier
[[thm-emg-local-classical-charged-scalar-development]], these periodic data
have a local solution of the full Einstein, sourced
Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations on
$(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Here $T_*>0$ is a width in the length
coordinate $x^0=ct$ (so the corresponding time width in seconds is $T_*/c$).
In its coordinate gauge, the first-order state lies in
$L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ with time derivative in
$L^\infty H^{s-1}$; the metric has
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and
$\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while
$F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and
$\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The Maxwell, scalar-potential,
metric-derivative, and harmonic constraints propagate. More generally, for
smooth data $(h,\mathcal K,e,b,A_\Sigma,\varphi_0,\pi_n)$ on any smooth
oriented three-manifold without boundary, define $F_\Sigma$ by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. The current authored supplier states local smooth development near each initial point, provided
$h$ is positive definite, $A_\Sigma$ is global,
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, the sourced Maxwell and
total-stress Einstein constraints hold, and $|\varphi|^2$ remains in
$\mathcal U$. Its uniqueness conclusion is local near the initial surface, up
to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry and electromagnetic
gauge $A\mapsto A+d\chi$,
$\varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi$ with $\chi|_\Sigma=0$ and
$[\chi]=\mathrm{Wb}$. This is a local conditional deduction in the adopted action
model. It asserts no nontrivial bundle sector, singular source, global-in-time
existence, geodesic completeness, empirical validity, or quantum field.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b>0$ have length units, let $\mathbf{x}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$, and define its Euclidean radius by $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. Take $a=b$ and $s=+1$ in the exact family of [[thm-emg-smooth-counterpoised-dust]], and define $H(\mathbf{x})=1+b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ on all of $\mathbb R^3$. For the family field strength $F$, set $n:=H\partial_0$, $e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i$, and define the static-frame electric components by $E_i:=cF(e_i,n)$ for $i=1,2,3$. This is an everywhere regular smooth solution with center values
$$H(0)=2,\qquad \nabla H(0)=0,\qquad \Delta H(0)=-\frac3{b^2},\qquad \rho(0)=\frac{3c^2}{32\pi G_Nb^2},\qquad S_g(0)=\frac3{4b^2},\qquad E_i(0)=0.$$
Its proper mass and signed charge are $c^2b/G_N$ and $Q_sc^2b/G_N$, respectively. The model density is positive everywhere, so its topological support, defined as the closure in $\mathbb R^3$ of $\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb R^3:\rho(\mathbf{x})\ne0\}$, is all of $\mathbb R^3$.

$$M=m,\qquad q_e=\sigma m,\qquad q_m=0,\qquad f(R)=\left(1-\frac mR\right)^2.$$

current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix $L>0$ and take the extremal RN datum with $M=q_e=L$, $q_m=0$, on $r>L$ in [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. For each dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define

$$\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=L+\lambda R,\ \omega),\qquad (T,R,\omega)\in\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2.$$

Writing $g_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ and $\mathcal F_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*\mathcal F$, one has

$$g_\lambda=-\frac{R^2}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT^2+\frac{(L+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+(L+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT\wedge dR.$$

As $\lambda\downarrow0$, these tensors converge in $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ on $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ to

$$g_0=-\frac{R^2}{L^2}dT^2+\frac{L^2}{R^2}dR^2+L^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_0=-\frac1L\,dT\wedge dR.$$

Under $T=L\tau$, $R=Lz$, the limiting datum is exactly the $f(z)=z^2$, $z>0$ product in [[def-emg-xs-br-products]], and it is a geometric electrovac datum by [[thm-emg-xs-br-verification]]. Here $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ means uniform convergence of every coordinate derivative on every compact subset in a finite smooth atlas. The convergence is only on $R>0$; no extension or convergence across $R=0$ is asserted.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $m_*>0$, $Q_e,\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$, and use [[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]] and [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] for the dyonic RN metric on $\mathcal M_J=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$, where $J$ is a connected open interval with $f(r)=1-2M/r+(q_e^2+q_m^2)/r^2>0$. The coordinate $x^0=ct$ and $r$ have units of metres. Put $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$; it is the future static Killing field on this region. Let $I_\gamma\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $\gamma:I_\gamma\to\mathcal M_J$ be a $C^2$ curve, and let $W$ be an open neighborhood of $\gamma(I_\gamma)$ carrying a dimensionless $C^2$ phase $\theta:W\to\mathbb R$. Set $k=d\theta$ and $K=k^\sharp$. Assume the eikonal equation $g^{-1}(d\theta,d\theta)=0$ holds throughout $W$, and that $K$ is nowhere zero and future directed along $\gamma(I_\gamma)$. Parameterize the phase ray by $\gamma'(\lambda)=K(\gamma(\lambda))$, which fixes its affine parameter normalization. For each spatial point $(r,\omega)\in J\times S^2$ and nonempty open interval $I\subset\mathbb R$, define the static observer curve $\sigma_{r,\omega}:I\to\mathcal M_J$ by $\sigma_{r,\omega}(s)=(s,r,\omega)$, where $s=x^0$ has units of metres. It is smooth and regular with tangent $\xi$, and it is future timelike because $g(\xi,\xi)=-f(r)<0$. Its proper-time parameter satisfies $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{f(r)}/c$ under the metric proper-time definition, so its normalized four-velocity is
$$U(r):=\frac{c}{\sqrt{f(r)}}\,\xi,\qquad g(U,U)=-c^2,\qquad \nu_U:=-\frac{k(U)}{2\pi}.$$
Here $U=d\sigma_{r,\omega}/d\tau$ is normalized by the SI proper-time convention of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], and $\nu_U$ is the phase frequency in cycles per unit ideal-clock time under [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. If $\gamma$ intersects static observer curves $\sigma_{r_E,\omega_E}$ and $\sigma_{r_R,\omega_R}$ at events $E$ and $R$, respectively, with $r_E,r_R\in J$, then the conditional model prediction is
$$\frac{\nu_R}{\nu_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_E)}{f(r_R)}}.$$
The phase data and source-free RN model are conditional inputs; the formula is not a reported observation or a claim of measured precision.

current_manifest_row.title: Classical configuration, cotangent phase and reference measures
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

current_manifest_row.title: Kinetic-plus-potential shell marginals and moments
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let integers $d,N\ge1$ satisfy $n=dN\ge3$. Choose a basis
$b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and the full-rank lattice
$\Lambda:=\sum_{i=1}^d\mathbb Zb_i$. The one-particle flat torus is
$Q:=\mathbb R^d/\Lambda$ with its quotient Euclidean metric and
translation-invariant volume $V:=|\det(b_1,\ldots,b_d)|$. Write
$\Lambda^N:=\Lambda\times\cdots\times\Lambda$ ($N$ factors) and set
$Q_N:=Q^N\cong\mathbb R^n/\Lambda^N$, whose position volume is $V^N$.
Use the global parallel cotangent trivialization $\Gamma_N\cong Q_N\times
\mathbb R^n$ and the product of quotient Lebesgue volume $dq$ with fibre
Lebesgue measure $dp$ in the canonical reference
$m_N=c_Ndq\,dp$ of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Let $m_j>0$ for
$1\le j\le n$, and let $U:Q_N\to\mathbb R$ be bounded with a smooth lift
$\widetilde U:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\widetilde U(x+\lambda)=\widetilde U(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$ and
$\lambda\in\Lambda^N$. Set
$$H(q,p)=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}+U(q),\qquad \alpha=n/2,\qquad C_m=\prod_{j=1}^n\sqrt{2m_j}.$$
Let $B_n$ be the Euclidean volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^n$. Fix
an energy $E$ that is a regular value of $H$ and whose shell
$\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$ is nonempty. For every continuous $g:Q_N\to\mathbb R$,
the coarea shell measure from [[thm-csm-regular-shell-coarea]] satisfies
$$\mu_E(g\circ\pi_N)=c_N C_m\alpha B_n\int_{Q_N}g(q)(E-U(q))_+^{\alpha-1}\,dq,$$
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$. Thus the position marginal of $P_E$ has density
proportional to $(E-U)_+^{\alpha-1}$. In the scaled momentum coordinates
$r_j=p_j/\sqrt{2m_j}$, the coarea shell measure over each $q$ with
$E>U(q)$ has fiber factor $dA_r/(2|r|)$ on the sphere
$|r|=\sqrt{E-U(q)}$. Define $\sigma_{E,q}$ as Euclidean surface area on
that sphere divided by its total area. It satisfies
$$\int \frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}\,d\sigma_{E,q}=\frac{E-U(q)}{n},\qquad \int \sum_j\frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}\,dP_E=\int(E-U(q))\,dP_E(q).$$
The result concerns the full kinetic-plus-potential shell; it does not replace
it by a shell of potential energy alone.

current_manifest_row.title: Canonical thermal preparation
current_manifest_row.statement:
For a fixed $N$, controls $\lambda$, measurable classical Hamiltonian
$H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, measurable for the
phase Borel sigma-algebra and taking energy values in joules, and the declared
physical reference measure $m_N^{\rm phys}$ of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], choose a prescribed
thermodynamic-temperature control $T>0$ in kelvins and
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ using the SI temperature convention of
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$0<Z_N(\beta,\lambda):=\int_{\Gamma_N}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}<\infty,$$
adopt the canonical state with density
$$\rho_{\beta,\lambda}=Z_N(\beta,\lambda)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}$$
relative to $m_N^{\rm phys}$. Set $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Normalizability
is a required condition on the chosen model; bounded-below energy alone does
not imply it. This probability law is an adopted preparation, not a
consequence of deterministic mechanics or evidence of laboratory
equilibration.

current_manifest_row.title: Grand canonical particle-exchange preparation
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $T>0$ be the prescribed temperature control in kelvins,
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and let the chemical-potential control $\mu$ have
units J per particle under the SI convention
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. In this adopted law, $\mu$ is the energy
coefficient conjugate to the dimensionless sector count $N$ in the weight
$e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}$; no derivative with respect to integer $N$ is used.
For $N\ge1$, let $\Gamma_N$ and its reference
measure be those of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], and let
$$H_N:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$$
be Borel measurable for the sector sigma-algebra
$\mathcal F_N$ generated by the open sets of $\Gamma_N$, with $+\infty$
marking forbidden states, and use the convention
$e^{-\beta(+\infty)}:=0$.
Define
the vacuum sector by $\Gamma_0=\{*\}$ with sigma-algebra
$\mathcal F_0=\{\varnothing,\{*\}\}$, reference mass
$m_0^{\mathrm{phys}}(\{*\})=1$, particle number $N=0$, and vacuum Hamiltonian
$H_0(*)=0$. On the disjoint union $\mathcal G:=\bigsqcup_{N=0}^\infty\Gamma_N$,
use the sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathcal G}:=\{A\subseteq\mathcal G:A\cap\Gamma_N\in\mathcal F_N\text{ for every }N\ge0\},$$
where $\mathcal F_N$ is the declared measurable structure on sector $N$, and
the reference measure
$$m^{\mathrm{phys}}(A):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(A\cap\Gamma_N).$$
This disjoint-union reference is sigma-finite because it is a countable sum
of the sigma-finite sector references, including the finite vacuum measure.
Let
$$\Xi(\beta,\mu):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty\int_{\Gamma_N} e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}$$
satisfy $0<\Xi<\infty$. Adopt the probability measure on
$(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_{\mathcal G})$ with density
$$\rho(N,z):=\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(H_N(z)-\mu N)}$$
relative to $m^{\mathrm{phys}}$. The finiteness condition is
part of the model; it requires control of the sector sum and is not implied
by each finite-sector partition function being finite. Particle-exchange
preparation is an assumption, not a deduction from fixed-$N$ dynamics. Under
the vacuum convention above, the $N=0$ contribution to $\Xi$ is exactly one.
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Classical particle exchange across countably many finite-N sectors at fixed temperature and chemical potential, only when the grand normalization converges.

current_manifest_row.title: Isothermal-isobaric joint preparation
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix integers $N,d\ge1$, a prescribed temperature control $T>0$ in kelvins,
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ as in [[def-td-si-quantities]], and external pressure
$P_{\rm ext}>0$ in J m$^{-d}$, a fixed dimensionless shape
$Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ that is Lebesgue measurable, meaning
$Q_1\in\mathcal L(\mathbb R^d)$, and has Lebesgue measure
$|Q_1|_d:=\lambda_d(Q_1)=1$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]), and
a positive volume reference $V_0$ in m$^d$. Write
$y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\in Q_1^N$, take $dy$ to be product Lebesgue measure on
$Q_1^N$, take $dp$ to be Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and take
$dV$ to be Lebesgue measure on $(0,\infty)$. Identify
the position domain at volume $V>0$ by $q_i=V^{1/d}y_i$. The Jacobian is
$V^N$, which is the full position-volume factor because $|Q_1|_d=1$. Adopt
the joint reference
$$d\nu_N=\frac{dV}{V_0}\,\frac{V^N\,dy\,dp}{N!a_0^{dN}},$$
where $a_0>0$ is the action reference in J s. The factors $dV/V_0$ and
$V^Ndy\,dp/a_0^{dN}$ are dimensionless. Let
$$H_N:(0,\infty)\times Q_1^N\times\mathbb R^{dN}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$$
be a product-measurable energy-valued Hamiltonian (in joules) for this
reference, with $+\infty$ marking forbidden states; set
$e^{-\beta(+\infty+P_{\rm ext}V)}:=0$. The product reference
$\nu_N$ is sigma-finite: $Q_1^N$ has finite measure, while $(0,\infty)$ and
$\mathbb R^{dN}$ have countable finite-measure exhaustions; the factor $V^N$
is finite on each set where $V$ is bounded. Assume
$$0<\Delta_N:=\int_0^\infty\!\int e^{-\beta(H_N(V,y,p)+P_{\rm ext}V)}\,d\nu_N<\infty.$$
Adopt the probability density
$$\rho_N(V,y,p):=\Delta_N^{-1}e^{-\beta(H_N(V,y,p)+P_{\rm ext}V)}$$
relative to $\nu_N$. The displayed
$N!$ is the single-species convention; for several indistinguishable species
with fixed counts $N_a$, replace it by $\prod_aN_a!$ as in
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. The factor $dV/V_0$ is an
explicit volume-reference convention; a different piston state measure gives
a different preparation. This postulate includes no piston kinetic energy
unless it is explicitly included in the Hamiltonian, and does not claim a
smooth wall dynamics.

current_manifest_row.title: Regular full-shell or finite-band preparation
current_manifest_row.statement:
For the full-shell branch, assume the Axiom of Choice required by the
mathematical supplier [[thm-csm-regular-shell-coarea]]. Let
$H:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ have a $C^2$ coordinate representative in every
canonical cotangent chart, and suppose there is an open interval $J\ni E$ on
which $dH\ne0$ and for which $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact whenever $K\subset J$ is
compact. For a nonempty regular shell
$\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, the cited theorem gives finite positive coarea mass
$0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$; adopt the microcanonical state
$$P_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$$
as the probability law for the specified preparation. Here $\mu_E$ is the
shell measure disintegrating the declared phase reference over energy; its
construction and hypotheses are exactly those in that theorem. The constant
$c_N$ in the mathematical reference is chosen to match the fixed-$N$ physical
reference of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]; the normalization
defining $P_E$ also cancels a common positive rescaling of that reference.

For a physical application, choose fixed conjugate reference scales
$\ell_j,p_{0j}>0$ in each cotangent chart, of the respective coordinate and
conjugate-momentum units, with $\ell_jp_{0j}=A>0$ the same action scale for
all $j$. For Cartesian positions these units are m and kg m s$^{-1}$;
other generalized coordinates have their own declared conjugate units. Put
$Q^j=q^j/\ell_j$, $P_j=p_j/p_{0j}$ and
$\widetilde H(Q,P)=H(q,p)$. These coordinates are dimensionless, while
$\widetilde H$ and $E$ remain in J. The actual reference Jacobian gives
$$dm_N^{\rm phys}=\frac{(A/a_0)^n}{\prod_sN_s!}\,dQ\,dP,\qquad n=dN.$$
Use this transformed constant in the shell theorem; in particular
$\mu_E^{\rm phys}(1)$ has units J$^{-1}$. The weighted shell area and
gradient are computed in these dimensionless coordinates, not by adding
squares of SI position and momentum derivatives of different dimensions.
The canonical forms pull back to $A\sum_jP_jdQ^j$ and
$A\sum_jdQ^j\wedge dP_j$. Thus physical time $t$ in seconds obeys
$$\frac{dQ^j}{dt}=A^{-1}\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H,\qquad \frac{dP_j}{dt}=-A^{-1}\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H.$$

the same time is $\widetilde H/A$, in s$^{-1}$. If one also chooses an
energy reference $E_*>0$ in J, then only with
$\widehat H=\widetilde H/E_*$ and $\tau=E_*t/A$ do the fully dimensionless
equations become $dQ^j/d\tau=\partial_{P_j}\widehat H$ and

the same trajectories and physical clock. It changes neither the adopted

fixed-$N$ reference of

coarea identity equally. This is a distinct finite-band
preparation, uniform relative to phase volume in the band. Restricting either
law to a dynamically accessible invariant subset or imposing further
conserved quantities defines another preparation and requires a separately
specified measure. Neither law nor ergodicity is deduced from deterministic
Hamiltonian evolution.

current_manifest_row.statement:
For the canonical preparation [[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], write
$H:=H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ for its measurable
Hamiltonian and $m:=m_N^{\rm phys}$ for its reference. With these data fixed
independently of $T$, let $Z(\beta)=\int e^{-\beta H}dm$ be finite and positive on an open
interval of $\beta>0$. If $H$ may equal $+\infty$, put
$S_H:=\{x:H(x)<\infty\}$, restrict $m$ to this measurable set, and evaluate
energy moments on $S_H$; the canonical weight is zero outside it, and the
restricted measure remains sigma-finite. In this statement $U$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(H)$ are the expectation and variance of $H|_{S_H}$.
Assume the
local envelope hypotheses of
[[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] hold for the finite-valued
statistic $X=H|_{S_H}$ and $\theta=-\beta$ on the restricted measure space.
Under the canonical preparation
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], the mean energy $U=\langle H\rangle$ obeys
$$\partial_\beta\log Z=-U,\qquad \partial_\beta U=-\operatorname{Var}(H),\qquad C_V:=\partial_TU=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(H)}{k_BT^2}\ge0,$$
where $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and $C_V$ is the model heat capacity at the fixed
controls. This is a finite-model response identity, not an empirical claim.

current_manifest_row.title: Ensemble entropy and potential identities
current_manifest_row.statement:
Adopt the canonical, grand and isothermal-isobaric preparations of
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], [[post-csm-grand-preparation]] and
[[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]]. Assume their positive finite normalizers,
finite first moments and integrable $\rho\log\rho$, and assume the local
parameter envelopes of [[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] for
each normalizer's sufficient statistics. If a Hamiltonian may be
$+\infty$, restrict its reference to the measurable set where it is finite;
the Gibbs density is zero off that set, and the restricted reference remains
sigma-finite. Thus every statistic passed to the exponential theorem is
finite real-valued. In each preparation, write $U:=\langle H\rangle$ for the
mean Hamiltonian; on the grand disjoint union let $\mathsf N$ be the sector
index and write $\bar N:=\langle\mathsf N\rangle$. Define the
reference-relative entropy by
$S=-k_B\int\rho\log\rho\,dm$ using the exact joint reference of each
preparation. Then the finite canonical free energy, grand potential and
isothermal-isobaric potential satisfy
$$F=-k_BT\log Z=U-TS,\qquad dF=-S\,dT$$
at fixed canonical model and reference;
$$\Omega=-k_BT\log\Xi=U-TS-\mu\bar N,\qquad d\Omega=-S\,dT-\bar N\,d\mu;$$
and, with $B=H+P_{\rm ext}V$,
$$G_{\rm isoP}=-k_BT\log\Delta=\langle H\rangle+P_{\rm ext}\langle V\rangle-TS, \qquad dG_{\rm isoP}=-S\,dT+\langle V\rangle\,dP_{\rm ext}.$$
For every normalized competing density $p$ with the same reference and the
finite energy and entropy conditions of
[[thm-csm-relative-gibbs-variational-principle]], one also has
$\langle H\rangle_p-TS[p]\ge F$, with equality exactly at the canonical
density almost everywhere.
The differentials hold at fixed remaining model data; integer $N$ is not a
differentiable variable. The identities do not assert thermodynamic-limit
equivalence or derive any preparation from ignorance.

current_manifest_row.title: Grand responses in beta and chemical potential
current_manifest_row.statement:
For the grand preparation [[post-csm-grand-preparation]], write
let $\mathcal G$ and $m^{\rm phys}$ be its disjoint-union state space and
reference, define $H(N,z):=H_N(z)$ on sector $\Gamma_N$, and define the
particle-number statistic $\mathsf N(N,z):=N$. Write $m_N$ for
$m_N^{\rm phys}$ in the sector sum, so
$$\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_N\int e^{-\beta H_N+\beta\mu N}\,dm_N.$$
Here $\beta>0$ and $\mu$ has units J per particle. Let
$S_H:=\{(N,z)\in\mathcal G:H_N(z)<\infty\}$, restrict $m^{\rm phys}$ to this
measurable set, and compute energy moments there; the grand weight is zero
outside it and the restricted measure is sigma-finite. Assume the local
envelopes of [[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] hold uniformly
on this restricted space for its finite-valued sufficient statistics $H$
and $\mathsf N$; expectations written $\langle N\rangle$ refer to
$\mathsf N$.
Then
$$\partial_\eta\log\Xi=\langle N\rangle,\quad \partial_\eta^2\log\Xi=\operatorname{Var}(N),\quad \eta=\beta\mu,$$
and, at fixed $\mu$,
$$-\partial_\beta\log\Xi=\langle H-\mu N\rangle,\qquad \partial_\mu\langle N\rangle=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N),\qquad \partial_\beta\langle N\rangle|_\mu=-\operatorname{Cov}(N,H-\mu N).$$
The covariance is computed in the full number-exchanging state. No
fixed-$N$ derivative or thermodynamic-limit identification is implied.

current_manifest_row.title: Isobaric volume and enthalpy fluctuations
current_manifest_row.statement:
For the joint preparation of [[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]], write $H=H_N$
for its Hamiltonian and set $B=H+P_{\rm ext}V$. Suppose the local
exponential envelopes hold for
$(B,V)$ on the measurable finite-energy set $S_H:=\{H<\infty\}$, with the
joint reference restricted to $S_H$. The Gibbs weight is zero off $S_H$;
there $B$ and $V$ are finite real-valued statistics and the restricted
reference remains sigma-finite. At fixed $T>0$ and $P_{\rm ext}>0$,
$$\partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\log\Delta=-\beta\langle V\rangle,\qquad \partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\langle V\rangle=-\beta\operatorname{Var}(V),$$
$$-\partial_\beta\log\Delta\big|_{P_{\rm ext}}=\langle B\rangle,\qquad C_P:=\partial_T\langle B\rangle\big|_{P_{\rm ext}} =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(B)}{k_BT^2}\ge0.$$
When $\langle V\rangle>0$, the model isothermal compressibility
$\kappa_T:=-\langle V\rangle^{-1}\partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\langle V\rangle$
equals $\beta\operatorname{Var}(V)/\langle V\rangle$. These are finite
preparation responses for the specified $dV/V_0$ reference; they need not
equal macroscopic response functions absent an additional limit argument.

current_manifest_row.title: Full ideal-gas shell moments and entropy conventions
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let integers $d,N\ge1$ satisfy $n=dN\ge3$. Take a flat one-particle torus
$Q=\mathbb R^d/\Lambda$, where $\Lambda=\sum_{i=1}^d\mathbb Zb_i$ for a
basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and
$V:=|\det(b_1,\ldots,b_d)|>0$, and set
$Q_N=Q^N\cong\mathbb R^n/\Lambda^N$, of position volume $V^N$. Use equal
masses $m>0$, Hamiltonian $H=\sum_{j=1}^np_j^2/(2m)$ and reference
$dq\,dp/(N!a_0^n)$ with fixed action scale $a_0>0$. For $E>0$, write
$\alpha=n/2$. The density of shell measure is
$$D(E)=\frac{V^N(2m)^{n/2}\alpha B_n}{N!a_0^n}E^{\alpha-1},$$
where $B_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^n$. Under the full
shell preparation, $K=E$ exactly and each quadratic momentum component has
mean $E/n$. Define the cumulative phase volume below energy $E$ by
$W(E):=m_N^{\rm phys}(\{H<E\})$. Choose an energy reference $E_0>0$ in
joules and a positive phase-volume reference $W_0$ in the same units as
$W(E)$. The reference $dq\,dp/(N!a_0^n)$ is dimensionless, so $W(E)$ and
$W_0$ are dimensionless and $E_0D(E)$ is dimensionless. The shell entropy
$S_{\rm sh}=k_B\log(E_0D(E))$ and cumulative volume entropy
$S_{\rm vol}=k_B\log(W(E)/W_0)$ have derivatives
$$\partial_E S_{\rm sh}=k_B\frac{\alpha-1}{E},\qquad \partial_E S_{\rm vol}=k_B\frac{\alpha}{E}.$$
They differ by $k_B/E$ at finite $n$; neither convention is selected by this
calculation.

current_manifest_row.title: Exact finite ideal-gas volume fluctuations
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $d\ge1$, $n=dN$, $m>0$, $a_0>0$, $V_0>0$, $T>0$ and
$P_{\rm ext}>0$. Use the unit-Lebesgue-volume shape $Q_1\subset\mathbb R^d$
and scaled coordinates $y\in Q_1^N$, $p\in\mathbb R^n$ of
[[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]], with physical positions
$q_i=V^{1/d}y_i$. Define the kinetic energy and Hamiltonian by
$$K(p):=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{p_j^2}{2m},\qquad H_N(V,y,p):=K(p).$$
In the adopted joint reference $dV/V_0$ times the scaled
position-momentum reference, the weight is $V^N e^{-\beta(K+P_{\rm ext}V)}$.
Its normalization is
$$\Delta_N=\frac{1}{V_0a_0^n} \left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{n/2} \frac{1}{(\beta P_{\rm ext})^{N+1}}.$$
The volume mean and variance and mean enthalpy are
$$\langle V\rangle=\frac{N+1}{\beta P_{\rm ext}},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V)=\frac{N+1}{(\beta P_{\rm ext})^2},\qquad \langle K+P_{\rm ext}V\rangle=\frac{n/2+N+1}{\beta}.$$
The extra one in the finite-$N$ volume factor follows from the stated
$dV/V_0$ prior; it is not a universal piston correction.

current_manifest_row.title: Finite-range lattice interaction and conditional energy
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$ and a finite nonempty alphabet $A$. A configuration is a function $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to A$. An interaction list consists of a finite index set $\mathcal R$ and, for each $r\in\mathcal R$, a finite nonempty shape $S_r\subset\mathbb Z^d$ containing $0$ and a function $\Phi_r:A^{S_r}\to\mathbb R$. The index $r$ is part of the data: two equal shapes with different indices represent two terms and are both counted. Every translate $x+S_r$ contributes once, with value $\Phi_r((\sigma_{x+y})_{y\in S_r})$.

The range is $R=\max_{r\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{diam}_\infty(S_r)$, with $R=0$ when $\mathcal R$ is empty. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, define the free-volume energy and the energy conditioned on an exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$ by
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}_\Lambda(\sigma)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:x+S_r\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi_r(\sigma_{x+S_r}),\qquad E_\Lambda(\tau_\Lambda\mid\eta)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:(x+S_r)\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\Phi_r((\tau_\Lambda\eta)_{x+S_r}).$$
Here $\tau_\Lambda\in A^\Lambda$, and $\tau_\Lambda\eta\in A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is the concatenated configuration equal to $\tau_\Lambda$ on $\Lambda$ and to $\eta$ on $\Lambda^c$.
These are finite sums: for each finite shape $S_r$, only finitely many anchors $x$ make $x+S_r$ meet $\Lambda$. Terms meeting $\Lambda$ but not contained in it appear in the conditional energy and not in the free-volume energy. The definitions are mathematical and assign no physical units; a physical model must state its units separately.

Level 0 — `thm-csm-ising-chain-convergent-series`: risk review complete. The exact periodic-chain supplier allows real J and beta>0 and gives lambda+>|lambda-|; at h=0 lambda+=2cosh K. Checked w=2sinh²(|K|/2)<8K²/9<2/9 for |K|<1/2 using log(4/3)>1/4. Finite geometric remainders integrate with error <=w^(n+2); domination by geometric powers gives absolute and compact-uniform convergence, including K=0 and negative J. Level 1 — `def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters`: risk review complete. Checked energy units J, beta in J^-1, a^d volume, entropy kB times nats, and h as spin energy bias. Level 1 — `lem-csm-chain-markov-bridge`: risk review complete. The positive symmetric 2x2 transfer matrix has lambda+ exceeding each diagonal: vector (c,lambda+-a) is positive and normalizable. Row normalization uses Tr=lambda+r and symmetry gives invariant pi=r². Summing both endpoints extends consecutive blocks to all finite coordinate sets; Countable Choice and the reviewed cylinder lemma give unique extension and stationarity. J=0 and h=0 remain positive matrices; this lemma alone does not assert the DLR property.

Level 1 — `lem-csm-gibbs-response-covariance`: risk review complete. Checked finite-sum derivatives with all real t and beta>0: Zprime=beta sum M weight and log Z second derivative beta² Var(M). Inverse-temperature signs give -mean H and positive Var(H). Constant observables and singleton sets give zero variance. Level 1 — `thm-csm-lattice-van-hove-pressure`: risk review complete. At fixed block side ell>2R leftover sites lie in the ell-boundary and have vanishing fraction on any van Hove sequence. Boundary-touching anchors contribute o(volume); seams contribute O(volume/ell), uniformly in spin assignment. Finite energy comparison bounds log Z by beta times energy error. First n then ell gives the same finite cubic limit, including empty interactions and singleton A; no continuum or long-range conclusion.

Level 2 — `thm-csm-lattice-dlr-existence`: risk review complete. The arbitrary finite-range specification hypothesis explicitly requires properness, consistency and cylinder-locality. Countable Choice gives subsequential measure compactness; for fixed Delta and cylinder C, gammaDelta C is a finite-coordinate function, so consistency passes to the limit without any exchange for general measurable functions. Equal probability measures on cylinders agree by pi-lambda; linear equations give convexity and local convergence gives closure. Any exhaustion and boundary sequence is allowed; no stationarity or uniqueness follows without later hypotheses.

Level 3 — `lem-csm-stationary-dlr-construction`: risk review complete. For a translation-invariant interaction, translating the finite conditional formula gives covariance, so every translate of a DLR law is DLR; finite averages use convexity. For fixed k, cube symmetric-difference/volume tends to zero by its explicit intersection formula. Cylinder subsequential compactness and closedness give a DLR limit; local expectations show shift invariance and cylinder uniqueness extends it to all events. Countable Choice inherited through the exact existence supplier; one initial witness needs no stronger choice. No ergodicity or uniqueness is asserted.

Level 3 — `thm-csm-chain-dlr-uniqueness`: risk review complete. The positive symmetric transfer matrix has explicit orthogonal spectral decomposition and |lambda-/lambda+|<1. Endpoint factors for a fixed observed block cancel in the normalized bridge; all four endpoint choices have positive leading denominators, giving uniform cylinder convergence even for negative J. The reviewed finite-range realization has onsite -h and pair -J terms. Existence gives a DLR subsequential limit equal to the Markov law; integrating the uniform boundary estimate forces every DLR state to agree on cylinders. No row-sum smallness is required; finite beta,J,h are essential.

Level 3 — `cex-csm-gibbs-marginals-not-free`: risk review complete. Directly checked the three-site sum: Z=2(2cosh K)^2 and endpoint correlation=tanh²K>0 for beta>0,J!=0, including negative J. Retaining only endpoints removes both bonds and gives uniform independent spins with zero correlation. Exact exponential positivity/strict monotonicity suppliers establish the strict sign. The refuted universal claim concerns unconditional marginals, whereas DLR uses conditional laws; no inconsistent-projective-family assumption is made.

Level 4 — `thm-csm-ising-low-temperature-coexistence`: risk review complete. Checked ray-parity cycle count: positive and negative crossings bound horizontal span, giving at most ell+1 candidate edges and 4*3^(ell-1) walks. Union bound and differentiated geometric series give delta=(4/3)r^4(5-4r)/(1-r)^2. For K>=2, exp(4)>437/9>48 makes r<1/16 and delta<1/2. The contour count translates to every interior site uniformly. Cylinder limits preserve magnetization bounds, spin reversal preserves the zero-field specification, and translation averages preserve both signs. Countable Choice is retained; no extremality or critical-temperature assertion occurs.

Level 4 — `thm-csm-lattice-dlr-variational-pressure`: risk review complete. Finite Gibbs relative entropy on each cube gives h-beta u<=p after the exact density/pressure limits. A DLR marginal is a mixture of boundary-conditioned laws. Bounded crossing energies differ from free energies by Dn=O(surface); comparing numerators and normalizers gives density ratio in exp(+-2beta Dn), also after mixing. Thus relative entropy/volume tends to zero and yields equality. Existence of a stationary DLR state establishes attainment. Empty interactions and singleton alphabets satisfy all limits. The converse maximizing=>DLR is expressly omitted.

Level 4 — `ex-csm-chain-analytic-interacting-model`: risk review complete. Checked exact chain hypotheses: d=1, h=0, finite beta>0, J>0 in joules and K=beta J dimensionless. The Markov bridge plus DLR uniqueness theorem, not the bridge alone, gives the unique DLR law; the exact series supplier restricts the expansion to 0<K<1/2. Countable Choice and adopted equilibrium interpretation are retained. The pressure is explicitly dimensionless and no finite sample, material calibration or equilibration claim is made.

Level 5 — `thm-csm-ising-coexistence-pressure-cusp`: risk review complete. For fixed beta,J with beta J>=2, pressure exists for every field by the bounded finite-range theorem. A zero-field stationary DLR law attains the variational value; the same stationary law remains an admissible competitor at h!=0 with u_h=u_0-hm. Dividing by negative h reverses the inequality. Opposite nonzero magnetizations separate positive and negative secant slopes, ruling out differentiability without requiring existence of one-sided derivatives or interchange with finite-volume derivatives. The proof does not locate a critical coupling.

The strict uniqueness condition and closed sufficient coexistence range K>=2 inherit the exact phase theorem, Countable Choice and adopted equilibrium postulate. Neither covers the intervening values; no exact threshold or measured transition is inferred. SI units make both displayed comparisons dimensionless.

current_manifest_row.title: Finite-alphabet product and probability compactness
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite nonempty set, and put $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$. Fix a bijection $(i_n)_{n\geq1}:\mathbb N_{>0}	o\mathbb Z^d$ and give $X$ the metric
$$d_X(\sigma,\eta)=\sum_{n\geq1}2^{-n}\mathbf 1_{\{\sigma_{i_n}
e\eta_{i_n}\}}.$$
For a finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $B\subseteq A^F$, write $[F,B]=\{\sigma\in X:\sigma|_F\in B\}$ and let $\mathcal C=\{[F,B]:F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d	ext{ finite},\ B\subseteq A^F\}$ be the cylinder algebra. A family $(
u_F)_{F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d	ext{ finite}}$ of probability measures on $A^F$ is **consistent** if $(\pi_E^F)_*
u_F=
u_E$ whenever $E\subseteq F$, where $\pi_E^F:A^F	o A^E$ is restriction. Such a family defines $\mu_0([F,B])=
u_F(B)$; consistency makes this a well-defined normalized finitely additive probability on $\mathcal C$. Then $X$ is compact, the Borel sigma-algebra is $\sigma(\mathcal C)$, and $\mu_0$ extends uniquely to a probability on $\sigma(\mathcal C)$. Moreover, every sequence of probabilities on this sigma-algebra has a subsequence whose cylinder probabilities converge to those of a probability measure; along that subsequence integrals of every continuous $f:X	o\mathbb R$ converge.

current_manifest_row.title: Unique interacting Ising state at sufficient high temperature
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, inverse temperature $\beta>0$, a constant finite field $h\in\mathbb R$, and symmetric pair couplings with zero diagonal, $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$ and $J_{ii}=0$, satisfying $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ for all $i,j,k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite integer $R\geq0$. For finite $\Lambda$, use the conditional energy
$$E_\Lambda(s_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}s_i,$$
where $\widehat s_i=s_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat s_i=\eta_i$ outside; let $\gamma$ be the corresponding finite-alphabet Gibbs specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. If
$$\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then there exists exactly one DLR state. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$ this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. It is not asserted to be sharp.

current_manifest_row.title: Stationary lattice entropy and energy densities
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $A$ be finite nonempty. A consistent translation-stationary family means probability measures $\nu_F$ on $A^F$ for every finite $F\subset\mathbb Z^d$, with $\nu_E=(\pi_E^F)_*\nu_F$ whenever $E\subseteq F$ and $\nu_{F+j}=(\tau_j)_*\nu_F$ for every $j\in\mathbb Z^d$, where $(\pi_E^F x)=x|_E$ and $(\tau_jx)_{i+j}=x_i$. This family extends to a unique translation-stationary probability $\mu$ on the cylinder sigma-algebra. Set $B_n=[-n,n]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$ for each integer $n\geq1$. For any such stationary $\mu$ and any bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction $(\mathcal R,(S_r,\Phi_r)_{r\in\mathcal R})$ as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], define
$H_n=-\sum_{\sigma\in A^{B_n}}\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)\log\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)$ with $0\log0=0$, and
$u(\mu)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\sum_{a\in A^{S_r}}\mu(\sigma|_{S_r}=a)\Phi_r(a)$.
Then
$$h(\mu)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{|B_n|}=\inf_{\ell\geq1}\frac{H_\ell}{|B_\ell|}$$
exists in $[0,\log|A|]$, and the free-boundary interaction-energy density satisfies
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E_\mu[H^{\rm free}_{B_n}]}{|B_n|}=u(\mu).$$

current_manifest_row.title: Peierls contour probability bound
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $B_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. For $s\in\{-1,+1\}^{B_n}$, set $\widehat s_i=s_i$ for $i\in B_n$ and $\widehat s_i=+1$ for $i\notin B_n$, and define
$$H_{B_n}^+(s)=-J\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\subset\mathbb Z^2:\ |i-j|_1=1,\ \{i,j\}\cap B_n\ne\varnothing}}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j,\qquad Z_{B_n}^+=\sum_{s\in\{-1,+1\}^{B_n}}e^{-\beta H_{B_n}^+(s)},\qquad \gamma_{B_n}^+(s)=(Z_{B_n}^+)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{B_n}^+(s)}.$$
The energy sum is finite because $B_n$ is finite and interactions are nearest-neighbor. For the nearest-neighbor Ising model with coupling $J>0$, zero field and $\beta>0$, any simple dual cycle $\gamma$ that occurs in the disagreement graph of a configuration determines the event $A_\gamma$ that all primal bonds crossed by $\gamma$ have disagreeing spins. Then
$$\gamma_{B_n}^+(A_\gamma)\leq e^{-2\beta J|\gamma|}.$$
For each such cycle, the parity-inside is defined by [[lem-csm-ising-parity-contours]] and lies in the variable box.

current_manifest_row.title: Conditional Ising equilibrium phase predictions
current_manifest_row.statement: Assume Countable Choice and adopt [[post-csm-interacting-equilibrium-gibbs]] for the specified classical Ising model. In the SI interpretation of [[def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters]], $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, $J$ is the coupling energy $J_{\rm I}$ in joules, and $h$ is an energy bias per dimensionless spin in joules, not a magnetic-field strength; hence $\beta J$ and $\beta h$ are dimensionless. The conditional model predictions are: (i) for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbor chain with finite $\beta>0$, $J,h\in\mathbb R$, the DLR equilibrium state is unique; (ii) for a translation-invariant finite-range Ising pair interaction with symmetric zero-diagonal couplings $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$, $J_{ii}=0$ and constant finite field, the sufficient condition $\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1$ gives a unique DLR equilibrium state; and (iii) for the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnet at $h=0$ and $\beta J\geq2$, there are distinct stationary DLR equilibrium states with opposite nonzero magnetization and the pressure is nondifferentiable in $h$ at zero. These deductions are restricted to the stated classical model; they do not report a measured transition or infer a phase diagram between the sufficient regimes.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete explicit compact-torus model and finite-chain verification; geometry, trigonometric regularity, and integration prerequisites are explicit.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix periods $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ and use the smooth quotient geometry and global
forms and vector fields supplied by
[[lem-emg-scaled-three-torus-smooth]]. In its coordinates set
$M:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb T^3_L$, with
$g=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2$, orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and time orientation
$N=\partial_0$. Fix $c,\mu_0>0$ as real coefficients and put

$$\widetilde f(x):=\cos\left(\frac{2\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad \widetilde h(x):=\frac{L_1}{2\pi}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi x^1}{L_1}\right).$$

These lifts on $\mathbb R^3$ are independent of $x^2,x^3$ and are
$\Lambda$-periodic. Let $f,h:\mathbb T^3_L\to\mathbb R$ be their unique
smooth descents, so $f\circ q=\widetilde f$ and $h\circ q=\widetilde h$.
The descended global vector field $\partial_1$ satisfies
$\partial_1h=f$ and $dh=f\,dx^1$. On the lifts,
$\widetilde h'=\widetilde f$ and
$\widetilde h(L_1,x^2,x^3)=\widetilde h(0,x^2,x^3)$. Define the smooth
current and field

$$j:=f\,\partial_0,\qquad F:=-\mu_0h\,dx^0\wedge dx^1.$$

Let $\iota_*:\mathbb T^3_L\to M$ be the slice inclusion
$y\mapsto(x^0_*,y)$, and let
$$T_3:=\{s\in\mathbb R^3:s_i\ge0,\ s_1+s_2+s_3\le1\}.$$
Orient the slice by the restriction of the global form
$dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.
Let $\theta:T_3\to\Delta^3$ be the affine identification
$\theta(s)=(1-s_1-s_2-s_3,s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Let $\Sigma$ be the oriented
spatial slice $x^0=x^0_*$, represented as a finite smooth singular chain as
follows. Triangulate the fundamental cube
$[0,L_1]\times[0,L_2]\times[0,L_3]$ by the six tetrahedra indexed by
$\sigma\in S_3$. The ordered vertices of tetrahedron $\sigma$ are
$0$, $L_{\sigma(1)}e_{\sigma(1)}$,
$L_{\sigma(1)}e_{\sigma(1)}+L_{\sigma(2)}e_{\sigma(2)}$, and
$(L_1,L_2,L_3)$. Let $\phi_\sigma:T_3\to\mathbb R^3$ be the affine map
taking $0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ to these ordered vertices; it extends affinely to
$\mathbb R^3$. Define the smooth singular simplex
$\psi_\sigma:=\iota_*\circ q\circ\phi_\sigma\circ\theta^{-1}:\Delta^3\to M$;
in the standard $T_3$ parameter it satisfies
$\psi_\sigma\circ\theta=\iota_*\circ q\circ\phi_\sigma$. It extends
smoothly to a neighborhood of $\Delta^3$ in its affine plane because
$\phi_\sigma$ extends affinely and $q,\iota_*$ are smooth. Put
$\Sigma:=\sum_{\sigma\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\psi_\sigma$.
Thus each simplex maps into the slice of $M$. The determinant of the
ordered edge vectors is $L_1L_2L_3\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$, so this
coefficient gives each simplex the cube orientation. The six regions are the
orderings $0\le u_{\sigma(3)}\le u_{\sigma(2)}\le u_{\sigma(1)}\le1$ of
$u_i:=x^i/L_i$; their interiors are disjoint and their union is the cube.
Internal faces cancel in pairs, and opposite cube faces are identified by
period translations with opposite boundary orientations, as verified below.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]
  \coordinate (O) at (0,0);
  \coordinate (X) at (2,0);
  \coordinate (Y) at (1,0.7);
  \coordinate (XY) at (3,0.7);
  \coordinate (Z) at (0,1.7);
  \coordinate (XZ) at (2,1.7);
  \coordinate (YZ) at (1,2.4);
  \coordinate (XYZ) at (3,2.4);
  \draw[thick] (O)--(X)--(XY)--(Y)--cycle;
  \draw[thick] (Z)--(XZ)--(XYZ)--(YZ)--cycle;
  \draw[thick] (O)--(Z) (X)--(XZ) (Y)--(YZ) (XY)--(XYZ);
  \draw[densely dotted,very thick] (O)--(XYZ);
  \node[below left] at (O) {$0$};
  \node[right] at (XYZ) {$(L_1,L_2,L_3)$};
  \node at (1.35,1.25) {six tetrahedra};
  \node[above] at (1.4,2.75) {$x^3=0\sim L_3$};
  \node[below] at (1.5,-0.42) {$x^1=0\sim L_1$};
  \node[right] at (3.55,1.3) {$x^2=0\sim L_2$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The perspective box depicts the fundamental cube, with opposite faces paired
by the labels. Its dotted body diagonal is the shared edge of the six affine
tetrahedra indexed by coordinate permutations. The drawing is schematic and
is not used in the chain-boundary proof above.

current_manifest_row.title: Adopted inertial velocity Langevin bath
current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], the filtered Brownian probability-space convention of [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]], and the adopted Newtonian spacetime and frame assumptions of [[post-cm01-frames]]. Fix one inertial frame $\Gamma=(o,u,(e_1,e_2,e_3))$ of that postulate: it is a fixed global adapted affine chart, with $o\in A$, $u\in V$, $\tau(u)=1$, and a fixed positively oriented $g$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the spatial displacement space $K=\ker\tau$. Its chart map assigns each event $p\in A$ the unique coordinates $(t_\Gamma(p),\mathbf x_\Gamma(p))$ satisfying $p=o+t_\Gamma(p)u+\sum_{i=1}^3x_{\Gamma,i}(p)e_i$. Let $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be the scalar position-coordinate process in this chart, measured in metres, whose value is the signed first spatial coordinate along the fixed axis $e_1$. The model tracks only $X$; it does not specify a full particle worldline or assert a law for either of the other spatial coordinates. Let $X_0$ be an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable real-valued random variable. On a measurable event $\Omega_*\in\mathcal F$ with $P(\Omega_*)=1$, assume $t\mapsto X_t(\omega)$ is continuously differentiable and define the velocity coordinate $V_t(\omega):=dX_t(\omega)/dt$ there, measured in metres per second. Thus $X_t=X_0+\int_0^tV_s\,ds$ on $\Omega_*$; values on the null complement do not affect the stochastic conclusions.

Take a primitive particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, a primitive constant bath temperature $T_b>0$ in kelvins, and the primitive SI Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin. The positive damping rate $\gamma$ is a primitive model parameter in seconds$^{-1}$; the positive noise amplitude $\sigma$ is derived as the square root of $2\gamma k_BT_b/m$ and has units metres seconds$^{-3/2}$. Let $B_t$ be standard scalar Brownian motion with $B_0=0$, variance $t$ in seconds, and future increments independent of the present filtration. Prepare an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable $V_0\sim N(0,k_BT_b/m)$ independently of future Brownian increments. The force $F:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is a prescribed deterministic locally continuous input in newtons. Adopt

$$V_t=V_0-\gamma\int_0^tV_s\,ds+\frac1m\int_0^tF(s)\,ds+\sigma B_t,\qquad \sigma^2=\frac{2\gamma k_BT_b}{m}.$$

The displayed integral equation is the definition of the stochastic differential notation $dV_t=-\gamma V_t\,dt+F(t)\,dt/m+\sigma\,dB_t$. Brownian increments have units seconds$^{1/2}$, so every term in the equation for $V_t$ has units metres seconds$^{-1}$. When $F=0$, the preparation is the stationary OU Gaussian law because its variance is $\sigma^2/(2\gamma)=k_BT_b/m$; the cited mathematical supplier establishes the specified OU model properties. The thermal noise normalization, Gaussian preparation, constant damping, and deterministic force coupling are adopted assumptions. No measurement, material calibration, nonlinear response, or microscopic derivation of this bath is asserted.

current_manifest_row.title: Exact OU velocity response, diffusion and Gaussian scaling
current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and the Brownian probability-space hypotheses in [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]]. Let $\gamma,m,\Theta,k_B>0$, $\sigma>0$, and $\sigma^2=2\gamma k_B\Theta/m$. Here these are real mathematical parameters; a separate physics postulate assigns their physical units and interpretation. Let $V_0\in\mathcal F_0$ satisfy $V_0\sim N(0,k_B\Theta/m)$ and be independent of future Brownian increments. For any locally continuous deterministic input $u:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, and every finite $t_f>0$, the equation restricted to $[0,t_f]$
$$V_t=V_0-\gamma\int_0^tV_s\,ds+\frac1m\int_0^tu(s)\,ds+\sigma B_t,\qquad 0\le t\le t_f,$$
has a unique continuous solution; these unique finite-horizon solutions agree on overlapping intervals and define one solution for all $t\ge0$. Its mean is
$$\mathbb E V_t=\frac1m\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}u(s)\,ds.$$
For $u=0$, $V$ is a stationary centered Gaussian process on $[0,\infty)$ with covariance
$$\mathbb E[V_sV_t]=v_\Theta e^{-\gamma|t-s|},\qquad v_\Theta:=k_B\Theta/m.$$
Define $Y_t:=\int_0^tV_s\,ds$ and $D:=v_\Theta/\gamma$. Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_t)=2v_\Theta\left(\frac{t}{\gamma}-\frac{1-e^{-\gamma t}}{\gamma^2}\right),\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Y_t)}{2t}=D.$$
For every deterministic input, the centered displacement $Y_t-\mathbb E Y_t$ is Gaussian with the variance above; consequently $(Y_t-\mathbb E Y_t)/\sqrt t$ converges in distribution to $N(0,2D)$. For constant input $u(s)=u_0$, $\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb E[V_t]/u_0=\chi:=1/(m\gamma)$ when $u_0\ne0$, and $D=\chi k_B\Theta$.

current_manifest_row.title: Conditional Langevin Green–Kubo and Einstein relation
current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the adopted velocity bath [[post-csm-dk-selected-thermal-langevin-bath]] on $t\ge0$ and the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let $X_t=X_0+\int_0^tV_s\,ds$ be the position coordinate in that model, and prepare $V_0$ in its specified stationary Gaussian law. For zero external force, define the stationary velocity covariance by
$$C_{VV}(\tau):=\mathbb E[(V_s-\mathbb EV_s)(V_{s+\tau}-\mathbb EV_{s+\tau})],\qquad s\ge\max(0,-\tau).$$
Stationarity makes it independent of $s$, and the model gives
$$C_{VV}(\tau)=\frac{k_BT_b}{m}e^{-\gamma|\tau|}.$$
For a deterministic force applied at time $s\le t$, the linear response kernel is
$$R_{VF}(t-s)=\frac1m e^{-\gamma(t-s)}=\frac{1}{k_BT_b}C_{VV}(t-s).$$
Here $R_{VF}$ is defined by the exact mean-response formula
$$\mathbb E[V_t]=\int_0^tR_{VF}(t-s)F(s)\,ds$$
for deterministic forcing from the stated zero-mean stationary preparation; its units are $\mathrm{kg^{-1}}$. The constant-force mobility below is a distinct steady-response coefficient.
The diffusion coefficient defined by centered displacement variance satisfies the Green–Kubo identity
$$D:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X_t-X_0)}{2t}=\frac{k_BT_b}{m\gamma}\quad\text{in }\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}.$$
More precisely, $D=\int_0^\infty C_{VV}(\tau)\,d\tau$.
The constant-force mobility
$$\mu:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E[V_t]}{F_0}=\frac1{m\gamma}\quad\text{in }\mathrm{s\,kg^{-1}}$$
for constant $F_0\ne0$. Hence $D=\mu k_BT_b$. The centered displacement divided by $\sqrt t$ converges in distribution to $N(0,2D)$. These are conditional model deductions, not observed transport data or a universal law for arbitrary systems.

current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], countable choice [[def-countable-choice]], and the rate model $E,\pi,w,Q$ of [[def-csm-dk-finite-reversible-rate-model]]. Let $X_t$ be the stationary two-sided chain of [[thm-csm-dk-nonexplosive-ctmc-and-gap]], with transition semigroup $P_t=e^{tQ}$. For any real observables $A,B:E\to\mathbb R$, write $A_c=A-\pi(A)$ and $B_c=B-\pi(B)$, and define
$$C_{BA}(t):=\langle B_c,P_tA_c\rangle_\pi,\qquad t\ge0.$$
Define $\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(A,B):=\pi(AB)-\pi(A)\pi(B)$, where $AB$ is pointwise multiplication.
For any finite horizon $t_f>0$, let $h:[0,t_f]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and let $\epsilon$ be dimensionless. For $0\le t\le t_f$, prescribe rates
$$w^\epsilon_{ab}(t)=w_{ab}\exp\! \left(\frac{\beta\epsilon h(t)}2(B_b-B_a)\right),\quad a\ne b,$$
with negative row sums on the diagonal, and let $p^\epsilon(0)=\pi$ evolve by the resulting finite forward equation. For $0\le t\le t_f$, the derivative of the observable mean at $\epsilon=0$ is
$$\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial\epsilon}\sum_a p^\epsilon_a(t)A_a\right|_{\epsilon=0}=\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds,\qquad R_{AB}(u)=-\beta\,\frac{d}{du}C_{BA}(u).$$
For a constant field $h$, define the normalized perturbed Gibbs vector by
$$\pi^\epsilon_a:=\frac{\pi_a e^{\beta\epsilon hB_a}}{\sum_{c\in E}\pi_c e^{\beta\epsilon hB_c}}.$$
It is stationary and its static susceptibility is $\beta h\,\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(A,B)$.

For any bounded vector observable $G:E\to\mathbb R^d$, set $G_c=G-\pi(G)$ and
$$C_{ij}(s):=\langle (G_c)_i,P_s(G_c)_j\rangle_\pi.$$
These correlations are absolutely integrable. The Green–Kubo covariance limit is
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(\int_0^T G(X_s)\,ds)}{2T}=D,\qquad D_{ij}=\int_0^\infty C_{ij}(s)\,ds=\langle (G_c)_i,(-Q)^{-1}(G_c)_j\rangle_\pi,$$
where $(-Q)^{-1}$ is the inverse on the mean-zero subspace and $D$ is positive semidefinite.

current_manifest_row.title: Conditional finite-bath equilibration and fluctuation response
current_manifest_row.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the adopted finite thermal rate model [[post-csm-dk-selected-reversible-bath-rates]], including its finite energy states, detailed-balance rates, temperature parameter and stationary Gibbs preparation for the response branch. For any initial microscopic probability law, the model's dimensionless relative information $\mathcal D(p_t\Vert\pi)$ is nonincreasing and tends to zero, and every bounded state observable has an almost-sure time average equal to its Gibbs mean. For real state observables $A,B:E\to\mathbb R$, any finite horizon $t_f>0$, and a continuous field $h:[0,t_f]\to\mathbb R$, the equilibrium-response branch with the postulated symmetric field-dependent rates has, for $0\le t\le t_f$, first-order response
$$\delta\langle A(t)\rangle=\int_0^t h(s)\left[-\beta\,\frac{d}{du}C_{BA}(u)\bigg|_{u=t-s}\right]ds,$$
where $\delta\langle A(t)\rangle:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\sum_a p_a^\epsilon(t)A_a\right|_{\epsilon=0}$, $p^\epsilon(0)=\pi$, and $p^\epsilon$ solves the finite forward equation for the postulated controlled rates. The correlation is $C_{BA}(u)=\langle(B-\pi(B)),P_u(A-\pi(A))\rangle_\pi$. For a constant field amplitude $g$ (in joules per unit of $B$), define the normalized perturbed equilibrium vector by $\pi^g_a:=\frac{\pi_a e^{\beta gB_a}}{\sum_{c\in E}\pi_c e^{\beta gB_c}}$ and define its susceptibility per unit field by $\chi_{AB}:=\left.\partial_g\pi^g(A)\right|_{g=0}$. Then $\chi_{AB}=\beta\,\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(A,B)$ and, when $g=\epsilon h$ for constant $h$, the derivative with respect to dimensionless $\epsilon$ is $h\chi_{AB}$. Here $\pi^g(A):=\sum_a\pi^g_aA_a$ and $\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(A,B):=\pi(AB)-\pi(A)\pi(B)$. If physical units are assigned to $A$ and $B$, write them as $[A]$ and $[B]$: $C_{BA}$ has units $[A][B]$, while $\beta h\,dC_{BA}/du$ has units $[A]$ per second, so the time integral and the derivative with respect to dimensionless $\epsilon$ have units $[A]$. These are conditional predictions of this finite stochastic model. They concern its dimensionless relative-information functional and state observables; no experimental observation, calibrated rate, material-specific claim or universal thermodynamic law is asserted.

current_manifest_row.title: Trace-class normal density states
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in its first argument. An operator $\rho\in\mathcal B(H)$ is a **density operator** when it is positive, trace class, and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Here trace class means compact with summable singular values, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the basis-independent trace of a trace-class operator.

The **normal density state represented by $\rho$** is the functional on bounded operators
$
\omega_\rho(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A),\qquad A\in\mathcal B(H).
$
In this page, “normal density state” means this specified trace-pairing representation; no equivalence with other definitions of normal functionals is assumed. The trace pairing is used only for bounded $A$. Unbounded observables are treated through their spectral probability measures in [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]].

current_manifest_row.title: Duhamel derivative and finite Kubo–Mori response
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.statement:
The path convention is $D\geq1$, an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, and a continuously differentiable map $M:I\to\operatorname{Herm}(D)$, where $\operatorname{Herm}(D)$ is the real vector space of Hermitian $D\times D$ matrices. For the control convention, $m\geq1$, $\theta\in\mathbb R^m$, and $M(\theta)=M_0+\sum_{a=1}^m\theta_aX_a$ with Hermitian matrices $M_0,X_1,\ldots,X_m$. At each control value let $Z=\operatorname{Tr}e^M$ and $\rho=e^M/Z$. For Hermitian $X$, define
$$\langle X\rangle_\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\rho(X):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(X-\langle X\rangle_\rho I)^2).$$
For Hermitian $X,Y$, put $\delta X:=X-\langle X\rangle_\rho I$ and $\delta Y:=Y-\langle Y\rangle_\rho I$, and define the Kubo--Mori covariance by
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho}(X,Y):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{1-u}\delta X\rho^u\delta Y)\,du.$$
For the static-control clause, take $H_0,B\in\operatorname{Herm}(D)$, $h\in\mathbb R$, $\beta>0$, and $H(h):=H_0-hB$.

Let $M(s)$ be a continuously differentiable path of Hermitian $D\times D$ matrices, $D\geq1$. Then
$
\frac{d}{ds}e^{M(s)}=\int_0^1 e^{(1-u)M(s)}M'(s)e^{uM(s)}\,du,\qquad
\frac{d}{ds}\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{M(s)}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_sM'(s)),
$
where $\rho_s=e^{M(s)}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{M(s)}$. For real controls $M(\theta)=M_0+\sum_a\theta_aX_a$ with Hermitian $X_a$,
$
\partial_a\log Z=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X_a),\qquad
\partial_a\partial_b\log Z=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{1-u}\delta X_a\rho^u\delta X_b)\,du,
$
where $Z=\operatorname{Tr}e^M$, $\delta X_a=X_a-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X_a)I$. The diagonal quadratic form of this Hessian is nonnegative. It equals the ordinary variance when $X_a$ commutes with $\rho$, and in general is bounded above by that variance. For $H(h)=H_0-hB$, $\beta>0$, and Hermitian $B$, the static susceptibility satisfies $\partial_h\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)=\beta\,\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0$. No infinite-dimensional or dynamical response is asserted.

More precisely, for every positive definite $\rho=e^M/\operatorname{Tr}e^M$ and Hermitian $X$, equality between the diagonal Kubo--Mori quadratic form and $\operatorname{Var}_\rho(X)$ holds if and only if $X\rho=\rho X$.
$
\frac{d}{dh}\langle B\rangle_{\rho_h}=\beta\,\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0,
\qquad \rho_h:=\frac{e^{-\beta H(h)}}{\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H(h)}}.
$
No infinite-dimensional or dynamical response is asserted.
