current_manifest_row.title: Trace-state cyclicity and spectral probability calculus
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.statement:
For a nonnegative countably additive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R$ with $\mu(\mathbb R)=1$, define
$$m(\mu):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu(\lambda)$$
when $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu(\lambda)<\infty$. If $\int\lambda^2\,d\mu(\lambda)<\infty$, then $|\lambda|\le(1+\lambda^2)/2$ makes the first absolute moment finite, and define
$$V(\mu):=\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m(\mu))^2\,d\mu(\lambda)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,d\mu(\lambda)-m(\mu)^2.$$
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space and $\rho$ a trace-class normal density state. Its positive eigenvalues $p_j$ and orthonormal eigenvectors $u_j$ satisfy $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$ in trace norm and $\sum_jp_j=1$. For bounded $A$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$, with absolute value at most $\|A\|$, and $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\operatorname{Tr}(A\rho)$. For a self-adjoint observable $A$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, the scalar law
$
\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\sum_jp_j\|E_A(B)u_j\|^2
$
is a probability measure. Its first absolute moment defines a scalar mean, and its second moment defines a variance; these are not defined as arbitrary unbounded products $\rho A$. For a fixed positive Boltzmann scale $k_B>0$ (in SI units J/K), the von Neumann entropy is $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_jp_j\log p_j\in[0,\infty]$, and need not be finite. Countable convex mixtures of normal density states converge in trace norm.

For this spectral law, the notations are $m_\rho(A):=m(\mu_\rho)$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\rho(A):=V(\mu_\rho)$.

current_manifest_row.statement:
**Input:** a nonzero finite-dimensional Hilbert space of dimension $d$, a Hermitian Hamiltonian matrix $K$, an inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ such that $H=\beta K$ is dimensionless, the ordered reference preparation $|\Phi_d\rangle$ from [[def-qsm-finite-gibbs-purification]], an output vector-error tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm out}>0$, and a rational amplification-failure target $0<\rho<1$. The input contract must also supply a rational shift-confidence target $0<\delta_{\rm sh}<1$, a finite call cap $Q_{\rm cap}$, and rational sampler precision $0<\nu\leq\delta_{\rm sh}^2/(10^{12}d(Q_{\rm cap}+1)^2)$ as required by [[lem-qa-30-spectral-minimum-shift]], as well as every sparse-oracle, block-encoding, controlled-evolution, inverse, norm-bound, energy-shift, coefficient-generation, implementation-error budget, synthesis-precision, reference-preparation, and cost object required by [[alg-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-purification]]. No matrix exponential, trace, exact spectral minimum, or gate is free input.

**Procedure:** invoke the normalized-output branch of [[alg-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-purification]] on $K$ with coefficient $\eta=\beta$, the stated vector-error and amplification-failure targets, the supplied shift-confidence target $\delta_{\rm sh}$, and complete access/cost certificates. Retain its frozen energy shift and all declared finite subroutines. Measure only its specified good/bad flag. On a good branch return the normalized system-reference vector; on a cap failure return the explicit output FAIL. If the certified shift event fails, do not assert the Gibbs approximation guarantee; any overall failure probability includes the supplied $\delta_{\rm sh}$ shift-confidence budget.

**Output:** either FAIL, or a normalized vector-register state in the successful branch, with the error and success guarantees supplied by [[thm-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-state-error-cost]]. An identity energy shift changes neither the normalized Gibbs density nor its canonical purification, since $e^{-(\beta K+cI)}=e^{-c}e^{-\beta K}$ and the trace is multiplied by the same scalar. This is a mathematical state-preparation procedure under the stated finite access model; it is not a physical bath or thermalization process.

current_manifest_row.title: Energy-band and grand quantum preparations
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Adopted finite-rank energy-band or commuting grand-canonical preparation for a nonzero model under the stated spectral, trace, and joint-moment conditions; infinite-rank band normalization and noncommuting energy-number ensembles are excluded.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix the positive Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in J/K and adopt two preparation rules within the normal-state model of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]].

**Energy-band preparation.** Let $H=H^*$ have spectral PVM $E_H$, and let $P=E_H(B)$ be a nonzero finite-rank projection for a specified Borel energy band $B\subseteq\mathbb R$. When the model declares preparation in this band without additional constraints, adopt the density $\rho=P/\operatorname{Tr}P$. This is a uniform preparation over the finite-dimensional range of $P$; it is not asserted for infinite-rank projections.

**Grand preparation.** Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space with a specified nonempty finite or countably infinite orthonormal basis $(u_j)_{j\in J}$, so its finite linear span is dense in $\mathcal H$. For each $\psi=\sum_{j\in J}c_ju_j\in\mathcal H$, define the diagonal self-adjoint energy and particle-number operators by
$$D(H)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|E_jc_j|^2<\infty\right\},\quad H\psi=\sum_jE_jc_ju_j;\qquad D(N)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|n_jc_j|^2<\infty\right\},\quad N\psi=\sum_jn_jc_ju_j,$$
where $E_j\in\mathbb R$ and $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. For chemical potential $\mu\in\mathbb R$, define the diagonal sum $K_\mu=H-\mu N$ by
$$D(K_\mu)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|(E_j-\mu n_j)c_j|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad K_\mu\psi=\sum_j(E_j-\mu n_j)c_ju_j.$$
This specifies the self-adjoint operator sum used in this postulate; on $D(H)\cap D(N)$ it agrees with the algebraic difference. Require $\inf_j(E_j-\mu n_j)>-\infty$. Fix $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$ and assume
$
0<\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_{j\in J} e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}<\infty.
$
Adopt the normal density $\rho_{\beta,\mu}=\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta K_\mu}$. For response claims, also require the uniform joint-moment envelopes in [[thm-tdmath-grand-response-covariance]]. Here $E_j,\mu$ are in J, $n_j$ is dimensionless, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ is in J$^{-1}$, and $\Xi$ is dimensionless.

These are adopted preparation assumptions, not consequences that a physical system is actually prepared in these states. They do not assert dynamical thermalization, an infinite-rank microcanonical state, or a grand ensemble for noncommuting $H,N$. The mathematical variational results to which they refer do not prove the physical postulate.

The self-adjointness assertions above are mathematical properties of the specified maximal diagonal domains. For a real sequence $(a_j)_{j\in J}$, let $M_a\psi=\sum_j a_jc_ju_j$ on $D(M_a)=\{\psi:\sum_j|a_jc_j|^2<\infty\}$. This domain contains the dense finite linear span. By definition, $\phi\in D(M_a^*)$ exactly when some $\eta\in\mathcal H$ satisfies $\langle M_a\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,\eta\rangle$ for every $\psi\in D(M_a)$, and then $M_a^*\phi=\eta$. Testing $\psi=u_j$ gives $\eta_j=a_j\phi_j$; hence $\eta\in\mathcal H$ forces $\sum_j|a_j\phi_j|^2<\infty$, so $\phi\in D(M_a)$. Conversely, if $\phi\in D(M_a)$, then for every $\psi\in D(M_a)$ the two inner products converge by Cauchy–Schwarz and satisfy $\langle M_a\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,M_a\phi\rangle$, since every $a_j$ is real. Thus $D(M_a^*)=D(M_a)$ and $M_a^*=M_a$. This applies to $a_j=E_j$, $a_j=n_j$, and $a_j=E_j-\mu n_j$.

current_manifest_row.title: Commuting quantum grand responses
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Conditional grand-canonical model for self-adjoint energy and nonnegative-integer number operators on a nonzero model with a nonempty common eigenbasis and local joint-moment envelope; noncommuting energy-number ensembles and experimental claims are excluded.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$, and let $H$ and $N$ be the diagonal self-adjoint energy and dimensionless particle-number operators with the domains specified by [[post-qsm-band-and-grand-preparation]] and common nonempty finite or countably infinite orthonormal eigenbasis $(u_j)_{j\in J}$ satisfying $Hu_j=E_ju_j$, $Nu_j=n_ju_j$, and $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. Let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$, let $\mu$ have units J, and let $(\beta,\mu)$ vary in an open parameter set $U$ where
$
0<\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_{j\in J}e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}<\infty.
$
On every compact subset of $U$, assume a summable envelope dominates
$
e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}(1+|E_j|^2+|n_j|^2)
$
uniformly in $j,\beta,\mu$. Under the commuting grand preparation of [[post-qsm-band-and-grand-preparation]], set $p_j=e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}/\Xi$ and write $\langle X\rangle=\sum_jp_jX_j$. Then, with the scalar-law variance defined by $\operatorname{Var}(N):=\sum_jp_j(n_j-\langle N\rangle)^2$,
$
\partial_\mu\log\Xi=\beta\langle N\rangle,\qquad
\partial_\mu\langle N\rangle=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N)\geq0,
\qquad
-\partial_\beta\log\Xi\big|_\mu=\langle H-\mu N\rangle.
$
In the natural parameters $(\theta_E,\theta_N)=(-\beta,\beta\mu)$, the Hessian of $\log\Xi$ is the covariance matrix of $(H,N)$, hence positive semidefinite. This result is conditional on the common eigenbasis and envelope; it does not cover noncommuting $H,N$, assert thermalization, or report measurements.

current_manifest_row.title: Static finite quantum response and covariance
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Nonzero finite-dimensional static canonical model with a bounded Hermitian control observable; noncommuting response uses Kubo–Mori covariance, while ordinary variance is asserted only in the commuting case.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Adopt the finite canonical state rule of [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]]. Let $H(h)=H_0-hB$ on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, where $H_0,B$ are Hermitian, $h$ is a real static control, $hB$ has units J, and $\beta>0$ is fixed in J$^{-1}$. Put $\rho_h=e^{-\beta H(h)}/Z(h)$. With $\delta B=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)I$, define
$
\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_h^{1-u}\delta B\rho_h^u\delta B)\,du.
$
Then the static susceptibility is
$
\frac{d}{dh}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0.
$
Here $\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_h}(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_h(B-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)I)^2)$ is the ordinary variance. The Kubo–Mori covariance equals this variance exactly when $[H(h),B]=0$; for noncommuting matrices the Kubo–Mori expression is the applicable covariance. This is a static model deduction, not a dynamical response or observation.

current_manifest_row.title: Pure entanglement and correlated mixtures
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Exact two-qubit state, marginal, entropy and sharp-observable probability calculations under the adopted normal-state Born interpretation; no apparatus or experimental outcome is asserted.
current_manifest_row.statement:
With $k_B>0$ as fixed by [[def-qsm-relative-entropy-domain]], for two qubits with basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, compare the Bell pure state $|\Phi\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2$, with density $\rho_\Phi=|\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|$, and the classically correlated mixture
$
\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}=\tfrac12|00\rangle\langle00|+\tfrac12|11\rangle\langle11|.
$
Both states have marginals $I_2/2$ and hence marginal entropy $k_B\log2$. The global entropies differ:
$
S(\rho_\Phi)=0,\qquad S(\rho_{\mathrm{mix}})=k_B\log2.
$
The Bell pure state is entangled for the declared two-qubit splitting; the mixture is separable. The dimensionless Hermitian observable $W=|00\rangle\langle11|+|11\rangle\langle00|$ has outcome $+1$ with probability $1$ in $\rho_\Phi$, and probabilities $1/2,1/2$ for $+1,-1$ in $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$. These are exact predictions of the adopted measurement model, not reports of an apparatus.

current_manifest_row.title: Two-level Gibbs and noncommuting susceptibility
current_manifest_row.design_state: draft-research
current_manifest_row.physical_scope: Exact finite two-level canonical model with a static transverse control; response is a model prediction and not an experimental measurement.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Take the two-dimensional Hilbert space with Hamiltonian $H(h)=\operatorname{diag}(-\epsilon/2,\epsilon/2)-h\sigma_x$, $\epsilon>0$, and $\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. The control $h$ has units J so that $h\sigma_x$ is an energy. At fixed $\beta>0$, put $Z(h)=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H(h)})$, $\rho_h=e^{-\beta H(h)}/Z(h)$, and define $\langle A\rangle_h:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hA)$. The finite canonical response is
$
\left.\frac{d}{dh}\langle\sigma_x\rangle_h\right|_{h=0}
=\chi=\beta\frac{\tanh x}{x},\qquad x=\frac{\beta\epsilon}{2}>0.
$
At $h=0$, the variance in the canonical state is $\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_0}(\sigma_x)=1$, so $0<\chi<\beta\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_0}(\sigma_x)=\beta$. The strict reduction from ordinary variance is a finite noncommuting quantum response; it makes no experimental claim.

current_manifest_row.title: Factorization of finite additive canonical densities
current_manifest_row.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Use the finite additive spectral data of
[[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. For every $N\ge1$,
$Z_N=Z_1^N$. For each product label $\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_N)$, the
diagonal entry of $\gamma_N$ is $\prod_{a=1}^N p_{j_a}$ and its off-diagonal
entries are zero. For each integer $k$ with $1\le k\le N$, write
$x,x'\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^k$ and $y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}$, and define the
first-$k$ reduced matrix $R_{N,k}$ by
$$ (R_{N,k})_{x,x'}:=\sum_{y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}}(\gamma_N)_{(x,y),(x',y)}. $$
When $k=N$, the tail-label set consists of the single empty tuple. Then
$R_{N,k}=\gamma_k$, where $\gamma_k$ is the diagonal matrix on
$V_k=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes k}$ with entries
$(\gamma_k)_{x,x}=\prod_{a=1}^k p_{x_a}$, and the canonical state has expected
additive energy $NE$.

current_manifest_row.title: Fixed-subsystem equivalence for independent finite energy shells
current_manifest_row.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix $q\ge1$, real one-site levels $e_j$, finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$, and
the ensembles of [[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. Suppose for
every $N$ the band width obeys
$$\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|,\qquad \delta_N/N\longrightarrow0.$$
Then every band is nonempty. For each fixed integer $k\ge1$ and $N\ge k$,
define $\sigma_{N,k}$ by its product-basis entries, for
$x,x'\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^k$,
$(\sigma_{N,k})_{x,x'}=\sum_{y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}}(\sigma_N)_{(x,y),(x',y)}$,
with a single empty tail label when $N=k$.
Define $\gamma_k$ to be the diagonal matrix on
$V_k=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes k}$ with entries
$(\gamma_k)_{x,x}=\prod_{a=1}^k p_{x_a}$ and zero off the diagonal. Then
$$\|\sigma_{N,k}-\gamma_k\|_1\to0,\qquad \frac1N s_N(\sigma_N)\to -\sum_{j=1}^q p_j\log p_j.$$
Here $\|D\|_1$ for a Hermitian finite matrix is the sum of absolute values
of its eigenvalues, and $s_N$ is dimensionless spectral entropy. This is an
independent finite-alphabet result; it asserts neither global trace-norm
convergence nor an interacting or continuous-model equivalence.

current_manifest_row.title: Local spin matrix algebras and their factor inclusions
current_manifest_row.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. An **infinite algebraic state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$.

For each finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$, the restriction $\omega|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ is a finite-matrix state. By [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], every positive normalized functional on a finite matrix algebra is represented by a unique density matrix. Define its **local density matrix** $\rho_\Lambda$ by

$$\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

where $\rho_\Lambda=\rho_\Lambda^*\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}\rho_\Lambda=1$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, the local densities are **consistent** when $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$, with partial trace characterized by its pairing against every $A\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. No density operator on a globally chosen Hilbert space is part of this definition.

This agrees with the canonical state convention of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]: the finite restrictions have norm one by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], giving $|\omega(A)|\le\|A\|$ on the dense local algebra and hence on its completion; evaluation at the norm-one identity gives $\|\omega\|=1$. Conversely a canonical state has local restrictions with density matrices of trace one, since the finite norm formula and continuity on the dense local algebra imply $\|\omega\|=\omega(I)$. No global density representation is asserted.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Set $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. A **smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle** is a smooth manifold $P$ with a smooth surjective submersion $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth right $U(1)$ action, and smooth local equivariant product charts $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times U(1)$; the action is free and transitive on each fibre. This is the smooth version of the right-action convention in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]. A **principal connection** on $P$ is a smooth distribution $H\subseteq TP$ with $T_pP=\ker(d\pi_p)\oplus H_p$ and $dR_z(H_p)=H_{pz}$. Equivalently, it is a smooth real one-form $\omega$ on $P$ that is right-invariant and satisfies $\omega(\zeta_P)=1$, where $\zeta_P(p):=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0}p\cdot e^{it}$; then $H=\ker\omega$. Choose a fixed smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle with a principal connection $\omega$. In a smooth trivialization $\tau_i:P|_{U_i}\to U_i\times U(1)$, set $\sigma_i(x):=\tau_i^{-1}(x,1)$ and $a_i:=\sigma_i^*\omega$. Choose the normalized local data $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]; the potentials used below are their rescalings $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$. On any overlap neighborhood admitting a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$, write $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. Use the dual representation $\rho_k(z):=z^{-k}$ and define charged scalar representatives by the global transition rule $\varphi_j=g_{ij}^{k}\varphi_i$, equivalently $e^{ikf_{ij}}\varphi_i$ on each phase-lift neighborhood; the connection rule there is

$$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0\,df_{ij}.$$

Here $\kappa_0>0$ is the chosen circle normalization with $[\kappa_0]=\mathrm{Wb}$, $k\in\mathbb Z$ is the representation weight, and $\lambda:=k/\kappa_0$ has units $\mathrm{Wb}^{-1}$. Because $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ and $k$ is an integer, the maps $g_{ij}^{k}$ satisfy the scalar transition cocycle. A charged scalar is a family of smooth local functions $\varphi_i$ satisfying this rule; all phase-lift calculations below are local, and no global phase lift is assumed. The constant $c>0$ is the length-to-time conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Define $F|_{U_i}:=dA_i$; the transition law gives $dA_j=dA_i$, so $F$ is a global curvature two-form. In a global real-potential model on a trivial bundle, one may instead take a global $A$ and any real $\lambda$; no charge quantization is imposed there.

In a local trivialization define the gauge-covariant derivative and its lower-index one-form by

$$P_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\partial_a\varphi_i-i\lambda A_{i,a}\varphi_i.$$

The transition laws give $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}P_{i,a}$, since $\lambda\kappa_0=k$. For any charged covector $Q_b$ with the same phase transition, define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative by $D_aQ_b:=\nabla_aQ_b-i\lambda A_aQ_b$ in a local trivialization; for a charged scalar $\eta$, set $D_a\eta:=\partial_a\eta-i\lambda A_a\eta$. Conjugate fields use the opposite gauge sign. Thus $D_aP_b$ is a well-defined charged covariant two-tensor, and $D_aP^a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. Consequently $|\varphi|^2$ and $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ are global scalar fields. Let $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth on an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$, write $V'$ for its ordinary real derivative, and choose a positive normalization constant $K_\varphi>0$.

The kinetic scalar $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ is real because its complex conjugate equals itself by symmetry of $g^{ab}$. Put

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

For SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[\varphi]=1$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[P_a]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[V]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}$; then $S_\varphi$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$. These are formal dimensional assignments, not measured values or physical postulates. On noncompact $M$, the integral is used when finite; otherwise only differences between configurations agreeing outside a compact set are defined, so every variation below is a compactly supported integral.

Allowed first variations are compactly supported smooth complex-section variations $\delta\varphi$, compactly supported real global one-form variations $\alpha=\delta A$ added to every local $A_i$ (so the same bundle transition functions are retained), and compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$. The formula defines a classical mathematical functional; it asserts no quantum interpretation, value of $\hbar$, or material-response model.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and let $\Phi$ be a translation-invariant uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For each finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, let $H_\Lambda$ be its free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian, $Z_\Lambda(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$, and $p_\Lambda(\beta)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$, where $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}$ is the ordinary finite-matrix trace of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Fix $\beta>0$, measured in inverse joules when the interaction terms are assigned energy units.

Write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$ for the lattice metric of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For a finite $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$. This minimum exists: $\Lambda$ is finite, so its complement is nonempty, and the distances from $x$ to that complement are positive integers. A sequence of finite nonempty regions $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove if $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n:=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Then $p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$ converges to the same finite value $p_\Phi(\beta)$ for every van Hove sequence; in particular, for positive integers $L$, the cube limit for $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ exists and equals this value. The normalization is dimensionless log-partition per lattice site; the finite-volume Helmholtz free energy per site is $-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$.

For every van Hove sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ and every sequence of self-adjoint matrices $B_n\in\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$ satisfying $\|B_n\|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$, the perturbed normalized log-partition functions satisfy
$$|\Lambda_n|^{-1}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta(H_{\Lambda_n}+B_n)}\right)\longrightarrow p_\Phi(\beta).$$
No spatial support condition on $B_n$ is needed. This theorem makes no claim for changes to the bulk interaction.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Fix an integer $d\geq1$, the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, and at each site the two-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H_i=\mathbb C^2$ with an orthonormal basis $e_{+1},e_{-1}$. Define the dimensionless local spin matrix $Z_i$ by $Z_i e_s=s e_s$ for $s\in\{-1,+1\}$. It is self-adjoint, diagonal in this basis, and has operator norm one. The local matrix algebras and factor inclusions are those of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], and the interaction/Hamiltonian convention is that of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

Let $J_{ij}=J_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ be specified for distinct sites, and let $h_i\in\mathbb R$. Assume there is a finite $R\geq0$ such that $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$, and
$$\sup_{i\in\Gamma}\left(|h_i|+\sum_{j\ne i}|J_{ij}|\right)<\infty.$$
The associated quantum interaction in the convention of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] is
$$\Phi(\{i\})=-h_iZ_i,\qquad \Phi(\{i,j\})=-J_{ij}Z_iZ_j\quad(i\ne j),\qquad \Phi(S)=0\ \text{for all other finite nonempty }S.$$
Its per-site norm sum is finite by the displayed bound, and all its terms are diagonal and commute. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, its free-boundary Hamiltonian is
$$H_\Lambda=-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_iZ_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,$$
where every unordered pair is counted once.

For a classical configuration $\sigma\in X:=\{-1,+1\}^{\Gamma}$, a finite region $\Delta\subset\Gamma$, and an exterior assignment $\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Delta^c}$, write $\widehat\sigma_i=\sigma_i$ for $i\in\Delta$ and $\widehat\sigma_i=\eta_i$ otherwise. The classical conditional energy is
$$E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)=-\sum_{i\in\Delta}h_i\sigma_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Delta\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat\sigma_i\widehat\sigma_j.$$
This is the finite-range conditional-energy convention of [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]: each interaction term meeting $\Delta$ is included once, including terms crossing its boundary. The sum is finite because $\Delta$ is finite and the interaction range is finite. Define the finite exterior boundary
$$C_\Delta:=\{j\notin\Delta:\text{there is }i\in\Delta\text{ with }J_{ij}\ne0\}.$$
It is finite, and $E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)$ depends on $\eta$ only through $\eta|_{C_\Delta}$.

For $\beta>0$ in inverse-energy units, set
$$Z_\Delta^\eta:=\sum_{\sigma_\Delta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Delta}}e^{-\beta E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)},\qquad \gamma_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta):=\frac{e^{-\beta E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Delta^\eta}.$$
The kernel sends an exterior configuration to a probability distribution on the spins in $\Delta$. A DLR measure for this model means a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ fixed by these kernels for every finite $\Delta$, in the specification terminology of [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. The finite kernel is defined without a choice principle; Countable Choice is stated separately when used to extend consistent cylinder probabilities to a measure.

The model is mathematical and supplies no measured coefficients. If interpreted with SI energy units, $J_{ij}$, $h_i$, $H_\Lambda$, and $E_\Delta$ are in joules, $\beta$ is in joules$^{-1}$, and $\beta E_\Delta$ is dimensionless.

The finite kernel requires no choice principle. Borel-measure extension from consistent cylinder probabilities uses [[def-countable-choice]].

current_manifest_row.title: Lattice Gaussian Riemann limits and the singular Bose endpoint
current_manifest_row.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $\alpha,\beta>0$, and $h>0$. Define
$F_B(p)=(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}$ for $p\ne0$ and
$F_F(p)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}+1)^{-1}$ for finite $\mu\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\mu<0$, both $F_B(\cdot;\mu)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}-1)^{-1}$ and $F_F$ are continuous, and for every fixed integer $s\ge0$ their polynomially weighted lattice sums converge with
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|hk|^sF(hk)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}|p|^sF(p)\,dp\quad(h\downarrow0).$$
The convergence is uniform when $(\beta,\mu)$ ranges over a compact subset of $\{\beta>0,\mu<0\}$ for bosons or $\{\beta>0,\mu\in\mathbb R\}$ for fermions. At the Bose endpoint $\mu=0$, define $F_B(p;0)=(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}$ for $p\ne0$. For every fixed $\beta,\alpha>0$ and $d\ge1$, monotone convergence gives $\int F_B(p;\mu)\,dp\uparrow\int F_B(p;0)\,dp$ as $\mu\uparrow0$, where the extended endpoint value is
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}F_B(p;0)\,dp=(\pi/(\beta\alpha))^{d/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^\infty\ell^{-d/2}\in(0,+\infty].$$
It is finite exactly when $d>2$. In that case the missing-origin lattice sums satisfy
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}}F_B(hk;0)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}F_B(p;0)\,dp\qquad(h\downarrow0).$$
No value is assigned to $F_B(0;0)$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5–3.6, thermodynamic momentum integrals and Bose/Fermi occupations
Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lectures 23–25, quantum gases and Bose condensation

current_manifest_row.strategy:
1.1 For $\mu<0$, the Bose denominator is bounded below by $e^{\beta(-\mu)}-1>0$ on compact sets; for finite $\mu$, the Fermi denominator is at least $1$. At large $|p|$, each occupation is bounded by $C e^{-c|p|^2}$ for positive constants $C,c$ depending on a compact parameter neighborhood. A polynomial factor $|p|^s$ is absorbed by a slower Gaussian because $r^s e^{-c r^2/2}$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$. Thus the continuum integrands and their polynomially weighted tails are integrable by comparison with products of one dimensional Gaussians and Tonelli [F3,F1]. For each fixed $h>0$, the max-norm shell $|k|_\infty=n$ has at most $C_dn^{d-1}$ points, and its summand is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $n$ times $e^{-c h^2n^2}$; the ratio of successive polynomial-Gaussian terms is eventually below a constant less than one, proving every lattice sum is finite. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

1.2 At $\mu=0$ and $p\ne0$, $e^x-1\ge x$ gives $F_B(p)\le(\beta\alpha|p|^2)^{-1}$. If $|k|_\infty=n$, the number of integer lattice points in that shell is $(2n+1)^d-(2n-1)^d\le C_dn^{d-1}$, while $|k|\ge n$. Hence for $0<h\le\delta$, $h^d\sum_{0<|hk|\le\delta}F_B(hk)\le C h^{d-2}\sum_{n\le\delta/h}n^{d-3}\le C'\delta^{d-2}$ when $d>2$; the last estimate follows by comparison on each unit interval with the integral of $x^{d-3}$ (and for $d=3$ the sum is bounded by a constant times $\delta/h$). The continuum small-ball integral has the same bound by decomposing into dyadic annuli, each with volume at most a constant times its radius to power $d$. [given, F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 On a fixed compact cube, uniform continuity of $|p|^sF(p)$ implies that replacing its value on each mesh cube by its value at the lattice corner changes the integral by at most the cube volume times the common modulus of continuity; summing finitely many cubes makes this error tend to zero. The measure of each mesh cube is $h^d$ by [F5]. This proves convergence on compact cubes. [step 1.1, F5, algebra]

3.1 To control tails uniformly for $0<h\le1$, let $Q_{k,h}=hk+[-h/2,h/2]^d$. For $p\in Q_{k,h}$, $|hk|^2\ge |p|^2/2-dh^2/4$. The Gaussian bound from step 1.1 therefore bounds each weighted lattice summand times $h^d$ by a fixed constant times the integral of a slower Gaussian over $Q_{k,h}$; the polynomial weight is absorbed by reducing its exponent once more. Cubes whose centers satisfy $|hk|>R$ lie outside the ball of radius $R-\sqrt d/2$. The integral of the slower Gaussian on that exterior tends to zero as $R\to\infty$, by [F1,F3]. Compact convergence from step 2.1 and this uniform tail bound prove the stated full-space limit and finiteness of every lattice sum. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F3, algebra]

4.1 Outside any fixed ball around zero, $F_B$ is continuous and has Gaussian tails, so the compact-annulus and tail argument in steps 2.1 and 3.1 applies. Split both the sum and integral into $0<|p|\le\delta$, $\delta<|p|\le R$, and $|p|>R$. First take $h\downarrow0$ on the annulus, then $R\to\infty$ using Gaussian tails, and finally $\delta\downarrow0$ using step 1.2. This proves convergence of the missing-origin Bose sums without assigning an origin value. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra]

5.1 For $p\ne0$, the positive geometric series gives $F_B(p;0)=\sum_{\ell\ge1}e^{-\ell\beta\alpha|p|^2}$. Its partial sums increase pointwise, so [F4] and Tonelli [F3] give the equality as extended nonnegative integrals $\int F_B=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\int e^{-\ell\beta\alpha|p|^2}dp$. The product Gaussian integral [F1] evaluates each term as $(\pi/(\ell\beta\alpha))^{d/2}$. The resulting positive series converges exactly when $d/2>1$, by comparison of $\sum\ell^{-d/2}$ with $\int_1^\infty x^{-d/2}dx$, and diverges otherwise. For $\mu<0$, $F_B(p;\mu)$ increases pointwise to $F_B(p;0)$ as $\mu\uparrow0$, so [F4] also gives convergence of the corresponding integrals to this endpoint value. This proves the extended endpoint formula, its divergence for $d\le2$, and the integral limit used by the Bose condensation theorem. [F1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

current_manifest_row.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the preparation postulate [[post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparation]], and the diagonal grand-trace hypotheses of [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]]. Let the mode set be finite or countable, with $0<q_j\le r<1$ and $\sum_jq_j^2<\infty$. Write $\bar n_j^B=q_j/(1-q_j)$ and $\bar n_j^F=q_j/(1+q_j)$. Then
$$|\bar n_j^B-q_j|\le\frac{q_j^2}{1-r},\qquad |\bar n_j^F-q_j|\le q_j^2.$$
The total mean occupations satisfy
$$\left|\sum_j\bar n_j^B-\sum_jq_j\right|\le\frac1{1-r}\sum_jq_j^2,\qquad \left|\sum_j\bar n_j^F-\sum_jq_j\right|\le\sum_jq_j^2.$$
The grand log partition factors, with $\Xi_B,\Xi_F$ as defined in [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]], obey
$$0\le -\log(1-q_j)-q_j\le\frac{q_j^2}{2(1-r)},\qquad 0\le q_j-\log(1+q_j)\le\frac{q_j^2}{2}.$$
Consequently,
$$\left|\log\Xi_B-\sum_jq_j\right|\le\frac1{2(1-r)}\sum_jq_j^2,\qquad \left|\log\Xi_F-\sum_jq_j\right|\le\frac12\sum_jq_j^2.$$
Thus the displayed linear fugacity terms approximate both total mean occupation and log partition with a controlled aggregate error under the stated squared-summability hypothesis.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5.1–3.5.2, Bose and Fermi occupation factors
Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lecture 23, quantum ideal gases

current_manifest_row.strategy:
1.1 For bosons, direct subtraction gives $\bar n^B-q=q^2/(1-q)$; because $q\le r$, this is nonnegative and at most $q^2/(1-r)$. For fermions, $q-\bar n^F=q^2/(1+q)$, which lies between zero and $q^2$. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 The identity $-\log(1-q)-q=\int_0^q x/(1-x)\,dx$ follows by integrating the derivative of $-\log(1-x)-x$ from zero. Since $1/(1-x)\le1/(1-r)$ on $[0,q]$, the integral is between zero and $q^2/[2(1-r)]$. Also $q-\log(1+q)=\int_0^q x/(1+x)\,dx$, whose integrand lies between zero and $x$, giving the Fermi bound $q^2/2$. [given, algebra]

2.1 Summing the nonnegative mode errors over any finite subset preserves these bounds. Taking the increasing limit over finite subsets gives the same inequalities for the total error because $\sum_jq_j^2<\infty$. [step 1.1, A1, algebra]

3.1 By [F1], the log partition function is the sum of the corresponding mode log factors. Sum the nonnegative factor remainders from step 1.2 over finite subsets and pass to the countable limit; squared summability makes each aggregate error finite and proves the claimed controlled first-order approximation. [step 1.2, F1, algebra] ∎

The occupation and log-partition errors are bounded explicitly. This is a controlled dilute or low-fugacity limit, not a high-temperature criterion, universality statement, interacting-gas result, or empirical observation.

current_manifest_row.statement: Take one dimensionless mode with fugacity $q=1/2$. The first-order dilute term for the mean occupation is $q=1/2$. As an explicit comparison, define the Poisson law by $P_q(n)=e^{-q}q^n/n!$ for $n\in\mathbb N_0$; its mean and variance are both $q$. The exact Bose law is geometric and the exact Fermi law is Bernoulli. This declared calculation illustrates the distinct occupation statistics and why a small-error conclusion needs a small-fugacity condition; the Poisson comparison is not asserted to follow from the linked theorem's mean and log-partition bounds.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5–3.6, Bose and Fermi occupations

current_manifest_row.strategy:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), $q=1/2$, and the exact occupation and variance formulas of [[pthm-qsm-dilute-occupation-limit]] and [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]].

[F1] [[pthm-qsm-dilute-occupation-limit]], Statement: Bose and Fermi mode means are $q/(1-q)$ and $q/(1+q)$, with explicit errors relative to $q$.

[F2] [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]], Statement: the one-mode Bose and Fermi variances are $q/(1-q)^2$ and $q/(1+q)^2$.

1.1 Substitution of $q=1/2$ gives $\bar n_B=1$, $\bar n_F=1/3$, while the first-order value is $1/2$. Thus the Bose error is $1/2$ and the Fermi error magnitude is $1/6$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 For the comparison law, $\mathbb E N=e^{-q}\sum_{n\ge1}nq^n/n!=q$ and $\mathbb E[N(N-1)]=e^{-q}\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)q^n/n!=q^2$, so $\operatorname{Var}(N)=q^2+q-q^2=q=1/2$. The exact variances from [F2] are $q/(1-q)^2=2$ for bosons and $q/(1+q)^2=2/9$ for fermions. These are finite exact model values; since $q$ is not near zero, no small-error claim follows from this example. [given, F2, algebra] ∎

current_manifest_row.title: A fixed-number constraint removes independent occupations
current_manifest_row.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
current_manifest_row.statement: Consider two bosonic modes with energies $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\mathbb R$ in J and inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$. Represent occupation outcomes by $(n_1,n_2)\in\mathbb N_0^2$ and define $N_i(n_1,n_2):=n_i$. Under a canonical preparation restricted to total number $N=N_1+N_2=1$, put $w_i=e^{-\beta\epsilon_i}$ and $p_i=w_i/(w_1+w_2)$; then the occupations satisfy $N_1+N_2=1$. For a grand-canonical comparison on these same two modes, choose chemical potential $\mu<\min(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ in J and put $q_i=e^{-\beta(\epsilon_i-\mu)}\in(0,1)$. The grand law has independent mode occupations, by factorization of its two geometric weights. This is the same product-law mechanism as in the linked periodic ideal model under its trace hypotheses.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §3.5, canonical and grand-canonical occupation sums

current_manifest_row.strategy:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), $\beta>0$, two finite energies, and the adopted canonical and grand preparations.

[A1] [[post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparation]]: fixed-number canonical preparation is the Gibbs state restricted to the selected number sector; grand preparation is a separate trace state.

[F1] [[pthm-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation]], Statement: occupations are independent in the diagonal grand state under its trace hypotheses.

1.1 The one-particle sector has exactly the two basis states $|1,0\rangle$ and $|0,1\rangle$, with weights $w_1,w_2$. Normalization gives probabilities $p_1,p_2$ with $p_1+p_2=1$, so $\mathbb E N_i=p_i$ and $N_1N_2=0$ in every canonical state outcome. [given, A1, algebra]

2.1 For the same two modes, the grand weights are $q_1^{n_1}q_2^{n_2}$, so $\Xi=(1-q_1)^{-1}(1-q_2)^{-1}$ and the normalized joint law is $\prod_{i=1}^2(1-q_i)q_i^{n_i}$ on $\mathbb N_0^2$; it is independent. The linked periodic theorem [F1] gives the same product law for its own modes under its trace hypotheses. By step 1.1, the fixed-number covariance is $\operatorname{Cov}(N_1,N_2)=\mathbb E(N_1N_2)-\mathbb E N_1\mathbb E N_2=-p_1p_2<0$. Thus the total-number constraint changes the joint law in this two-mode model, without implying any general finite-volume ensemble-equivalence failure. [step 1.1, F1, algebra] ∎

current_manifest_row.title: Trace-class bounded-observable response
current_manifest_row.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ be a densely defined operator with domain $D(H)$, and let $\hbar>0$. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$. Let $\rho$ be a density operator, meaning a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$ as in [[def-qsm-density-trace-state]], and assume $\rho U_0(t)=U_0(t)\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Let $A,B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be bounded self-adjoint operators, let $T>0$ be a finite time in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Interpret $H$ in J, $\hbar$ in J s, and $h(t)B$ in J; if $A,B$ carry units $[A],[B]$, then $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

Define $B_s=U_0(s)^*BU_0(s)$, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and
$$
R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\rho[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac2{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.
$$
The trace-class interaction-picture solution of $\rho_I'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}[B_t,\rho_I(t)]$, $\rho_I(0)=\rho$, satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),
$$
where $|r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}/2$ for $0\le t\le T$. Thus the bounded-observable first variation is exact, with an explicit finite-time remainder. No energy or entropy moment of $\rho$ is assumed, and no trace of an unbounded product such as $\rho H A$ is used.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.2
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, complete lecture notes, §3.3.11–3.3.12

Under the finite-dimensional unitary dynamics of [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]], let $P_E$ be the orthogonal spectral projection of $H$ for its distinct energy $E$. For every density matrix $\rho$,

$$\frac1T\int_0^T U(t)\rho U(t)^*\,dt\longrightarrow\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$

in trace norm as $T\to\infty$. The diagonal energy blocks, including all blocks within degenerate eigenspaces, remain. This is Cesaro convergence of the averaged state; pointwise convergence of $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ is not asserted.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Use the finite energy basis, energies $E_a$, rates $w_{ab}$, Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$, and jump matrices $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. Define $R:=\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=\sum_a r_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and the no-click matrix $K:=-iH_{\rm s}/\hbar-R/2$. The **specified energy-resolved instrument** has the following outcomes:

1. If the current state is the energy eigenstate $|a\rangle$, then during a no-click interval of length $t$ the unnormalized state is $e^{tK}|a\rangle$.
2. In an infinitesimal interval $dt$, the outcome labelled $a\to b$ has jump operation $\sqrt{dt}\,L_{ab}$ and probability $dt\,\langle a|L_{ab}^*L_{ab}|a\rangle+o(dt)$. Its normalized post-click state is $L_{ab}|a\rangle/\|L_{ab}|a\rangle\|=|b\rangle$.
3. The no-click operation over $dt$ is $M_0(dt)=I+Kdt+o(dt)$. Since $K^*+K=-R$ and $\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=R$, the no-click and jump effects sum to $I+o(dt)$.
4. After each recorded jump, repeat the same rule from the new energy label.

The output path records the current label $a(t)\in E$. This is one selected instrument model; the one-time GKSL semigroup alone does not specify a unique record process.

current_manifest_row.physical_scope: For a finite-dimensional subsystem represented by H=C^d (d>=1), the chosen thermal GKSL state law and energy-resolved instrument apply physically only on the declared finite interval [0,t_res], where t_res>0 is in seconds. All-time limits are mathematical continuations of the same fixed generator and instrument, with no physical-applicability claim beyond t_res. No microscopic bath limit, calibrated rate, or reported measurement is asserted.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.5.3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ be finite and let the modeled subsystem Hilbert space be $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$. A state is a dimensionless matrix $\rho=\rho^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ such that $x^*\rho x\geq0$ for every $x\in\mathbb C^d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. An initial preparation is a chosen state $\rho_0$. Let $H_{\rm s}=H_{\rm s}^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, $m\geq0$ finite, have units seconds$^{-1/2}$. We adopt the time-independent finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]],

$$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm s},X]+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(L_jXL_j^*-\frac12\{L_j^*L_j,X\}\right),$$

where $[U,V]=UV-VU$ and $\{U,V\}=UV+VU$. The exact state law is

$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_t=\mathcal L(\rho_t),\qquad \rho_{t=0}=\rho_0,\qquad \rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0,\qquad 0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}.$$

Here $t_{\rm res}\in(0,\infty)$ is the finite resolved duration, in seconds, adopted for this model. For mathematical long-time calculations, the same constant generator defines the continuation $e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0$ for every $t\geq0$; this continuation makes no physical-applicability claim for $t>t_{\rm res}$. By [[thm-qsm-dt-gksl-sufficient]] it is a density-state evolution on that mathematical continuation as well.

Let $k_{\rm B}>0$ denote Boltzmann's constant, with SI units joules per kelvin; it converts absolute temperature to an inverse-energy parameter. Let $T_{\rm bath}>0$ be the adopted absolute temperature parameter in kelvins and set $\beta:=(k_{\rm B}T_{\rm bath})^{-1}$, with units joules$^{-1}$. The temperature and rates are model inputs here; no measured calibration is asserted. The temperature parameter alone imposes no detailed-balance condition on an arbitrary choice of $L_j$. When the generator is specialized to the connected Gibbs-jump model, its energies, $\beta$, and rates must satisfy the hypotheses in [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]].

Within this effective formulation, the dimension $d$, preparation $\rho_0$, general coefficient matrices $H_{\rm s}$ and $L_j$, positive constants $\hbar$ and $k_{\rm B}$, temperature $T_{\rm bath}$, and resolved duration $t_{\rm res}$ are primitive, adopted model inputs with the types and units stated above; none is derived here from a microscopic reservoir or inferred from a measurement. This status is local to this formulation, not a claim that each is fundamental in every physical theory. The space $\mathbb C^d$, inverse-energy parameter $\beta$, generator $\mathcal L$, and state family $\rho_t$ are derived by their displayed constructions once those inputs and the physical state-law postulate are fixed. The selected Hermitian observable $A$ and its unit assignment are additional adopted observable data; its expectation is derived by the trace formula below.

In the connected Gibbs-jump parameterization, the orthonormal energy basis, real level energies $E_a$ in joules, and rates $w_{ab}\geq0$ in seconds$^{-1}$ are instead the adopted primitive spectral and rate data, subject to the Gibbs-balance and connectivity hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. In that parameterization the operator coefficients are derived as $H_{\rm s}=\sum_a E_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$; they replace, rather than supplement, the independent general matrix choices above. The Gibbs weights $\pi_a=e^{-\beta E_a}/\sum_b e^{-\beta E_b}$ are derived, while the energy-resolved instrument remains a separate adopted assumption. In particular, neither the temperature nor the Gibbs-balance relation derives the numerical rates.

For that Gibbs-jump specialization, record predictions additionally adopt the particular ideal energy-resolved instrument defined in [[def-qsm-dt-monitored-chain]], and only on $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$ as a physical model. Its law for all $t\geq0$ is used only as a mathematical continuation when deriving a long-time coefficient. A one-time channel family alone does not select this record law. Full [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is retained as the formal set-theoretic premise in the monitored-chain supplier's construction of the joint path law; it is not a physical postulate about nature. A selected observable is represented by a Hermitian matrix $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ with its assigned physical units, and its model expectation $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)$ has those same units; no measurement outcome is reported.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume full AC, [[post-qsm-dt-effective-bath]], and the finite connected Gibbs-jump model with its selected energy-resolved instrument. Prepare the system with diagonal Gibbs law $\pi$. Assign a real pointer velocity $v_a$ in metres per second to each recorded energy label, with $\sum_a\pi_av_a=0$, and define the model record displacement $Y_T=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}\,ds$. The postulate's physical applicability is limited to $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$. For formulas at arbitrary $T\geq0$ and their limit, continue the same finite-rate chain as an idealized mathematical model; this gives no physical-applicability claim for $T>t_{\rm res}$. Thus the displayed formula is a conditional physical-model prediction for $0\leq T\leq t_{\rm res}$ and a mathematical model identity for all $T\geq0$ in the continuation:

$$\mathbb E_\pi[Y_T]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)=2\int_0^T(T-s)C_v(s)\,ds,$$

where $C_v(s)=\sum_a\pi_av_a(e^{sW}v)_a$. The limit

$$D_{\rm rec}:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C_v(s)\,ds=\langle(-W|_{\pi^\perp})^{-1}v,v\rangle_\pi\geq0$$

exists and has units square metres per second. This long-time limit is a derived coefficient of the idealized mathematical continuation. It is not a measurement of a system's position, a calibrated material coefficient, or evidence that the microscopic bath obeys the effective model.

current_manifest_row.title: Reference-wall normalization preserves proper thermal and particle ratios
current_manifest_row.design_state: Finite static cavity reference point sets the selected Killing lapse to one and rescales finite charge while preserving proper-temperature and proper-particle-energy ratios; inputs remain draft.
current_manifest_row.statement:
Use the static subcase, finite coordinate slab, and open chart domain $U$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. Adopt that lemma's SI convention: $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$, the spatial coordinates $x^i$ are in metres, $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and the metric components and length-normalized Killing field are dimensionless. Let $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ be future timelike and orthogonal to the coordinate slices, and put $\mathcal N_\xi(q):=\sqrt{-g_q(\xi_q,\xi_q)}>0$ and $u_q:=\xi_q/\mathcal N_\xi(q)$ for $q\in U$. Let $W\subset U$ be a specified smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold whose induced metric has signature $(-,+,+)$ (a timelike cavity wall), and choose a reference event $q_{\rm ref}\in W$ in the static region. Put $\mathcal N_{\rm ref}:=\mathcal N_\xi(q_{\rm ref})>0$, which is dimensionless in this convention. No asymptotically flat end is assumed. Supply a function $\vartheta:U\to(0,\infty)$ assigned units kelvins and interpreted as the local proper temperature measured by observer field $u$, and a covector field $p$ on $U$ whose components have units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. When a particle-energy interpretation is used, supply a vector field $P$ on $U$ that is future-directed and causal and satisfies $p_q=g_q(P_q,\cdot)$ at each $q\in U$; its components then have the same units as $p$ because the metric is dimensionless. Define, pointwise on $U$, $\mathcal T_\xi(q):=\mathcal N_\xi(q)\vartheta(q)$ and $E_\xi(p;q):=-c\,p_q(\xi_q)=-c\,p_a(q)\xi^a(q)$. Rescale the generator by $\widehat\xi:=\xi/\mathcal N_{\rm ref}$. The reference lapse is then $\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(q_{\rm ref})=1$, while the normalized temperature and particle-energy ratios at every $q\in U$ are unchanged:
$$\frac{\mathcal T_{\widehat\xi}(x)}{\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(x)}=\frac{\mathcal T_\xi(x)}{\mathcal N_\xi(x)}=\vartheta(x),\qquad \frac{E_{\widehat\xi}(p;x)}{\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(x)}=\frac{E_\xi(p;x)}{\mathcal N_\xi(x)}=-c\,p_a(x)u^a(x).$$
For each slice charge defined in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]], $H_{\widehat\xi}=H_\xi/\mathcal N_{\rm ref}$. current_manifest_row.statement:
On a nonempty open region of the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian model of [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], assume an actual solution of its source-free stress and particle balances and corrected relaxation law. Use the state maps and units of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with smooth future unit observer congruence $u$ (the frame, not a chart or tetrad), $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $n,T,c>0$, positive $C^1$ coefficient fields $\zeta,\tau$, and $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. Require enough regularity that all displayed balances and the entropy-current divergence are classical. The solution remains in the application's declared open near-equilibrium regime. With
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,$$
the exact pointwise identity is
$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\geq0.$$
This is conditional on an actual solution and does not assert general solution existence.

There is also an explicit homogeneous solution under the additional application condition that the declared open regime contains constant zero-gradient reference data with $\Pi=0$. Let the selected material's state domain contain $(v_0,\sigma_0)$ with $n_0=1/v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_0)>0$, and let the regime contain those constant state data. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, choose constant positive $\zeta_0,\tau_0$ and set $u=\partial_{x^0}$. For some $\delta>0$ seconds take the open region $O=(-c\delta,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$, put $t=x^0/c$, and define
$$\Pi(t)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0},\qquad t> -\delta.$$
Choose $\Pi_0$ sufficiently small that the full field and first-derivative data stay in the declared regime throughout $O$. Then the source-free balances and corrected law hold, and the entropy production is strictly positive at every finite $t\geq0$ when $\Pi_0\ne0$, and zero when $\Pi_0=0$.

The argument is a conditional model deduction, not an observation or a general nonlinear existence, causality, or stability theorem. No empirical premise is used.

current_manifest_row.title: Causal solutions, Killing horizons, escape and metric extensions

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision
references.locator: Causal structure and stationary black-hole terminology; the selected-model escape observable, signed normalization and well-definedness are specified locally below.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time orientation. All definitions below are mathematical. A solution of a specified covariant field system is a tuple of fields of the regularity stated by that system satisfying its equations on its stated domain; this terminology alone supplies neither existence nor a global electromagnetic potential.

**(a) Global causal and Cauchy conventions.** Use exactly [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]: a future causal curve is locally absolutely continuous in coordinate charts, has nonzero future causal derivative almost everywhere, and has no constant subinterval. Inextendibility and causal reachability $J^\pm$ have that item's endpoint-extension meanings. A Cauchy set meets every inextendible causal curve at exactly one parameter value: its inverse image under each such curve is a singleton, as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. A spacelike hypersurface is a smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold with positive-definite induced metric; this local condition does not assert the global Cauchy property. Strong causality has the small-neighborhood no-leaving-and-reentering meaning of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]. Global hyperbolicity means strong causality and compactness of every $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$, exactly as there; no equivalence theorem is added here.

**(b) Null and Killing horizons.** A smooth embedded hypersurface $H\subset M$ is **null** when $g|_{TH}$ is degenerate. Equivalently, for any local defining function $f$ with $H=\{f=0\}$ and $df\ne0$ on $H$, $g^{-1}(df,df)=0$ on $H$. A specified smooth vector field $\xi$ is **Killing** when $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, equivalently $\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$, using [[def-gr-killing-field]] and [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. A **Killing horizon for $\xi$** is a null hypersurface whose nonzero-generator part $H_*:=\{p\in H:\xi_p\ne0\}$ is nonempty and dense in $H$, and on that part the specified field is tangent, null and normal: $\xi_p\in T_pH$ and $g(\xi_p,X)=0$ for every $X\in T_pH$. A generator parameter or asymptotic normalization, when required, must be specified separately.

On $H_*$ the **signed surface gravity** for this precise $\xi$ is the unique smooth scalar $\kappa_H$ such that

$$d\bigl(g(\xi,\xi)\bigr)_p=-2\kappa_H(p)\,\xi^\flat_p\quad(p\in H_*).$$

This is an equality of ambient covectors at points of $H$, not merely of their pullbacks to $TH$. No constancy or positivity is asserted. Under a nonzero constant rescaling $\xi'=a\xi$, $\kappa'_H=a\kappa_H$. A **bifurcation surface** is a specified smooth spacelike two-surface $B$ where the extended Killing field vanishes and the specified horizon branches meet (or have $B$ as their common boundary). Surface gravity at such a surface means a smooth extension of the scalar from the adjacent nonzero-generator portions, with each point in their closure, only if that extension exists; the defining equation at $\xi=0$ alone determines no value. Neither a bifurcation surface nor such an extension is asserted to exist.

**(c) Sections, area and ergoregions.** A **horizon section** is a specified smooth spacelike embedded two-surface $S$ in the horizon, with positive induced metric $h$. Its area density is $\mu_h=\sqrt{\det(h_{ij})}\,|dy^1dy^2|$ of [[def-riemannian-volume-density]]. Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for intrinsic density integration, as in [[def-riemannian-volume-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]. Its possibly infinite area is the nonnegative extended value

$$\operatorname{Area}_g(S):=\sup\left\{\int_S\chi\mu_h:\chi\in C_c^\infty(S),\ 0\le\chi\le1\right\}\in[0,+\infty],$$

with the extended order of [[def-extended-reals]]. On compact $S$ this is $\int_S\mu_h$; orientation is unnecessary. The density glues by [[lem-the-riemannian-volume-density-is-coordinate-independent]]. A stationary field here is a specified Killing field timelike on a specified nonempty open region; no normalization is inferred from this adjective. Its **ergoregion** in the chosen model is $\{g(\xi,\xi)>0\}$, its **stationary-limit set** is $\{g(\xi,\xi)=0\}$, and its **ergosurface** is the relative boundary of its ergoregion. Every ergosurface point lies in the stationary-limit set; the converse requires a separate sign-change argument. Nullness, Killing-horizon status and escape-boundary status are separate claims; a coordinate root alone proves none of them.

**(d) Selected-model escape.** Fix a specified open spacetime model $U\subseteq M$ and specified smooth radius observable $r:U\to\mathbb R$. An admissible escape path is a continuous $\gamma:[0,T)\to U$, $0<T\le+\infty$, with $\gamma(0)=p$, such that every compact parameter segment has a finite subdivision on whose pieces the coordinate curve is $C^1$, with nonzero future causal tangent (one-sided at piece endpoints). Define

$$\mathcal E_{U,r}:=\left\{p\in U:\exists\gamma\text{ admissible from }p\ \forall R>0\ \exists t\in[0,T):r(\gamma(t))>R\right\}.$$

The **selected escape boundary** is $\partial_U\mathcal E_{U,r}$. This explicitly selected piecewise-$C^1$ path class is contained in the global causal-curve class of (a); it does not replace that class in Cauchy definitions. No geodesic restriction, conformal completion, event-horizon identification or maximal extension is implicit in this definition.

**(e) Approached metric extensions and curvature obstructions.** A $C^2$ nondegenerate metric extension of an open model $(U,g)$ consists of a smooth Hausdorff second-countable four-manifold $\widetilde M$, a $C^2$ Lorentz metric $\widetilde g$ of the same signature, and a smooth open embedding $j:U\to\widetilde M$ with $j^*\widetilde g=g$. An **approached added point** is $p\in\widetilde M\setminus j(U)$ with $j(x_n)\to p$ for a specified sequence $x_n\in U$ (or the corresponding limit of a specified curve). An **extension obstruction at that approach** means no such extension and added point can realize the stated approach. In particular, unbounded absolute values of a polynomial complete contraction of the curvature tensor and metric inverse along $x_n$ obstruct such an approached $C^2$ nondegenerate extension. This criterion concerns curvature without its covariant derivatives. A smooth metric extension is the same definition with smooth $\widetilde g$. These notions alone assert neither a distributional matter source nor geodesic incompleteness.

**(f) Observers and spatial fields.** Observers, smooth observer congruences and their integral curves, adapted charts and tetrads retain the distinct meanings of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Relative to a future unit observer $n$, an electric or magnetic spatial covector is identified with a spatial vector only by raising with the positive rest metric $h=g+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ on $n^\perp$. Such spatial vectors $e,b$ are not tetrad basis vectors. No singular-source product or action is defined by this vocabulary.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $U$ be a coordinate neighborhood whose image in $\mathbb R^4$ is star-shaped about the origin, and let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$ with $dF=0$. In those coordinates define

$$A_a(x):=\int_0^1 t x^b F_{ba}(tx)\,dt.$$

Then $A$ is a smooth one-form on $U$ and $dA=F$ there. This is a local potential statement only.

For the gauge assertion, let $g$ be a smooth Lorentz metric on a neighborhood of a smooth spacelike hypersurface patch $S$, and let $A$ be a smooth one-form already defined on that neighborhood. Near each point of $S$ there is a smaller neighborhood and a smooth scalar $\chi$ such that

$$A':=A+d\chi,\qquad dA'=dA,\qquad \nabla^aA'_a=0.$$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the symmetric-hyperbolic supplier [[thm-gr-local-symmetric-hyperbolic-well-posedness]]. The gauge proof constructs local Gaussian-normal coordinates with $x^0=0$ on the slice, $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, and $(g^{ij})$ positive definite. No global potential or global gauge choice is asserted. When the Lorenz condition is combined with the Maxwell equation for a potential, [[prop-emg-potential-ricci-wave-identity]] retains the Ricci term.

current_manifest_row.title: Charged particle and Liouville data on a stationary Lorentzian domain

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity lecture notes, §4.3.2, Killing fields and conserved particle quantities
Igor Bogush, Kirill Kobialko and Dmitri Gal’tsov, Constructing massive particles surfaces in static spacetimes, arXiv:2402.03266v1, §II

current_manifest_row.statement:
Use SI dimensions and the signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Take the geometric data of
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]: $O$ is a nonempty connected open domain in a
smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$, $\nabla$ is the
Levi–Civita connection, and $\xi$ is a smooth future-directed timelike Killing
field with dimensionless components in physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$
and $x^i$ measured in metres. Put $N:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and
$u:=\xi/N$, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its smooth
tangent-bundle data carry the supplier's explicit foundational assumption
[[def-countable-choice]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$); no stronger choice principle
is added here.

Let $A$ be a smooth real one-form on $O$: for each $x\in O$, $A_x:T_xO\to\mathbb R$
is linear, and in every smooth chart $(x^a)$ its coefficients $A_a$ are smooth
and obey the covector transformation law $A'_i=A_a\,\partial x^a/\partial y^i$
on an overlapping chart $(y^i)$. The coefficients have units tesla metres.
Define $F$ in each chart by
$$F_{ab}:=(dA)_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a.$$
This prescription defines a global smooth antisymmetric covariant two-tensor:
under a change of chart $x=x(y)$ the chain rule gives
$$F'_{ij}=F_{ab}\,\frac{\partial x^a}{\partial y^i}\frac{\partial x^b}{\partial y^j},$$
since the only additional term is
$A_a(\partial_i\partial_jx^a-\partial_j\partial_ix^a)=0$. Thus $F=dA$ is a two-form;
its components have units tesla. A global gauge compensator is a smooth real
function $\Lambda_\xi$ on $O$ satisfying
$$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi,\qquad (\mathcal L_\xi A)_a:=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b$$
in every smooth chart. This defines the Lie-derivative coefficients globally:
under $x=x(y)$, put $J^a_i:=\partial x^a/\partial y^i$ and
$K^i_a:=\partial y^i/\partial x^a$. Substitution of
$A'_i=A_aJ^a_i$ and $\xi'^i=K^i_a\xi^a$ gives
$$ (\mathcal L_\xi A)'_i=\xi^b(\partial_bA_a)J^a_i+\xi^bA_aK^j_b\partial_jJ^a_i+A_cJ^c_j(\partial_iK^j_b)\xi^b+A_bJ^a_i\partial_a\xi^b. $$
Differentiating $J^c_jK^j_b=\delta^c_b$ and using
$\partial_jJ^a_i=\partial_iJ^a_j$ cancels the two middle terms, leaving
$(\mathcal L_\xi A)'_i=(\mathcal L_\xi A)_aJ^a_i$. The units of
$\Lambda_\xi$ are
tesla metres. Define contraction by
$(\iota_\xi F)_a:=\xi^bF_{ba}$ and set
$$\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi,\qquad \Phi_\xi:=-c\Psi_\xi.$$
Thus $\Psi_\xi$ has units tesla metres and $\Phi_\xi$ has units volts.

Let $c>0$ be the speed of light, let $m>0$ be a particle rest mass in
kilograms, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be its charge in coulombs, and put
$M:=mc^2>0$ joules. A charged massive Lorentz trajectory is a $C^2$ curve
$x:J\to O$, where $J$ is an open real interval, parametrized by physical
length $s_m=c\tau$ in metres, with future unit tangent
$w:=dx/ds_m$, $g(w,w)=-1$, energy four-vector $P:=Mw$, and equation
$$\nabla_wP^a=cqF^a{}_bw^b,\qquad F^a{}_b:=g^{ac}F_{cb}.$$
In particular $g(P,P)=-M^2$ and $P$ is future directed. This is a conditional
definition of curves satisfying the equation; it makes no existence claim.

The future massive shell for this definition is the subset
$$\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future directed}\}.$$
On the full tangent bundle $TO$, define charged transport as the vector field
whose integral curves, with parameter $\lambda=s_m/M$, satisfy
$$\frac{dx^a}{d\lambda}=P^a,\qquad \nabla_{dx/d\lambda}P^a=cqF^a{}_bP^b.$$
In a smooth chart its expression is
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}:=P^a\partial_{x^a}+\left(-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c+cqF^a{}_bP^b\right)\partial_{P^a}.$$
The restriction of this field to $\mathcal P_M^+(O)$ is justified by
[[lem-tgr-charged-liouville-preserves-mass-shell]]. For any smooth real scalar
$\zeta$ and smooth vector field $\beta$ with components in inverse joules,
define the dimensionless charged exponential ansatz on the shell by
$$f(x,P):=\exp\!\left(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\right),\qquad \beta_b:=g_{bc}\beta^c.$$
The equation $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ means that the derivative of this function
along the restricted charged transport vector field vanishes.

Under a smooth gauge change $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, with $\chi$ in tesla square
metres, the corresponding compensator changes by
$\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. These definitions fix the sign
convention for $F$, the Lorentz force, and the potential terms used on this
page.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $L>0$ be a length in metres and $T_K>0$ a reference temperature in kelvins. On the connected open Rindler domain $O=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(0,\infty)_x\times\mathbb R_y\times\mathbb R_z$, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the metric

$$ds^2=-\left(\frac{x}{L}\right)^2(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2.$$

Choose the future direction of increasing $x^0$ and the Killing field $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$. The selected lapse is $N(x)=x/L$. Define $\beta_K:=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and adopt the stationary-bath temperature field $T(x)=T_KL/x$, so the inverse-temperature vector is $\beta=\beta_K\xi=\xi/(k_BT_K)$. For the global-stationarity input of [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], use an auxiliary neutral species with rest mass $m>0$, charge $q=0$, chemical potential $\mu=0$, global potential $A=0$, and compensator $\Lambda_\xi=0$. This auxiliary kinetic sector is a supplier hypothesis for the finite-cell construction; it is not identified with the two quantum cells.

Set $x_1:=L$, $x_2:=2L$ and place the cells at $p_i:=(x^0=0,x=x_i,y=0,z=0)\in O$, as in the placement map of [[post-tgr-selected-gibbs-kms-preparation]]. For $t_K,\tau\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\gamma_i(t_K):=(ct_K,x_i,0,0),\qquad \Gamma_i(\tau):=(c\tau/N_i,x_i,0,0).$$
Here $t_K$ is the Killing-flow parameter in seconds and $\tau$ is proper time in seconds. Each $\gamma_i$ is a smooth future-directed timelike integral curve of $c\xi$ through $p_i$; since $N_i=x_i/L$ is constant on it, $\Gamma_i(\tau)=\gamma_i(\tau/N_i)$ and $g(d\Gamma_i/d\tau,d\Gamma_i/d\tau)=-c^2$. Thus $\tau=N_it_K$ is the proper-time relation on the two worldlines. For each $i\in\{1,2\}$ take $\mathcal H_i=\mathbb C^2$ with an orthonormal basis $\{|0_i\rangle,|1_i\rangle\}$, let $Q_i=0$, and set

$$H_i=\Delta_i|1_i\rangle\langle1_i|,\qquad \Delta_i>0\text{ joules}.$$

Set $q=0$ for the cells and use $\mu_i=0$. Then $N_1=1$, $N_2=2$, $T_1=T_K$, and $T_2=T_K/2$. With $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$, the exact local partition functions and states are

$$Z_i=1+e^{-\beta_i\Delta_i},\qquad \rho_i=\frac{|0_i\rangle\langle0_i|+e^{-\beta_i\Delta_i}|1_i\rangle\langle1_i|}{Z_i}.$$

The total state and Killing-time generator are

$$\rho=\rho_1\otimes\rho_2=\frac{e^{-\beta_K(H_1+2H_2)}}{Z_1Z_2},\qquad G_K=H_1+2H_2.$$

This is a positive normalized finite-dimensional state. It is $\beta_K$-KMS for the Killing-time dynamics and its $i$th cell state is $\beta_i$-KMS for the local proper-time dynamics of [[pthm-tgr-local-kms-clock-temperature]]. The equality $N_iT_i=T_K$ is exact within this constructed model; no observation, material-realization claim, infinite-volume limit, or interaction between cells is asserted.

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), §1.6, printed pp. 23–25.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ be a coordinate neighborhood in an oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, foliated by spacelike $s$-levels. Write
$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $D$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$, define $\operatorname{div}_h v:=D_iv^i$ and $(\operatorname{curl}_h v)_i:=\epsilon_i{}^{jk}D_jv_k$, and define the spatial cross product by $(u\times v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$ in this frame. For a smooth real two-form $F$, define the real spatial components $e_i:=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$; thus $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$ in the adapted tetrad. Assume the source-free model of draft definition [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], whose actual equations are $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=0$; its draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1].

The six evolution equations for $(e,b)$ have principal part
$$n(e)-\operatorname{curl}_h b=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b),\qquad n(b)+\operatorname{curl}_h e=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b).$$
For a spatial covector $\xi$, let $C(\xi)v:=\xi^\sharp\times v$ in the oriented orthonormal frame. Set $\theta^0:=\alpha ds=-g(n,\cdot)$ and decompose any spacetime covector as $\zeta=\zeta(n)\theta^0+\zeta_\perp$, where $\zeta_\perp(n)=0$ and $|\zeta_\perp|_h$ is its spatial norm. The spatial principal block is the linear map on $\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3$ defined by $S(\xi)(u,v)=(-C(\xi)v,C(\xi)u)$. It is real symmetric, has eigenvalues $0,0,|\xi|,|\xi|,-|\xi|,-|\xi|$, and satisfies $\|S(\xi)\|=|\xi|$. Therefore the principal symbol $P(\zeta)=\zeta(n)I_6+S(\zeta_\perp)$ is positive definite for every covector with $\zeta(n)>|\zeta_\perp|_h$. In the adapted coordinates its time matrix is $\alpha^{-1}I_6$, and every coordinate spatial matrix is symmetric. Derivatives of the frame and metric enter only as smooth lower-order coefficients depending on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,e,b)$; in a first-order metric state they are zero-order terms. The remaining two Maxwell equations are the constraints $\operatorname{div}_h e=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_h b=0$.

current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric covariant tensor $K$, and smooth spatial vectors $e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, use signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and suppose the four Einstein–Maxwell constraints of [[thm-emg-gauss-codazzi-maxwell-constraints]] hold. In SI convention use length coordinate $x^0=ct$, dimensionless $g,h$, $K$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $e=E/c$, $b=B$ in tesla. Reconstruct the complete initial two-form on $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ by
$$F(N,\mathsf e_i)=-e_i,\qquad F(\mathsf e_i,\mathsf e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k,$$
where $N$ is the future unit normal symbol and $(\mathsf e_i)$ is a positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame. Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local source-free Einstein–Maxwell development on an open variable-width neighborhood of the entire initial surface. After restriction to a smaller collar, the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry carrying $F$ to $F$. There is no uniform positive time width for noncompact $\Sigma$ and no global-in-time conclusion.
